title: [InsertSync] temporary sibling-subview non-overlap assumption for issue #499
body:
## Summary
- Add a temporary InsertSync policy for issue #499: treat **sibling subviews** (cut from the same parent tile) as non-overlap in local-memory alias analysis.
- Keep **parent-child** alias handling unchanged (still conservative).
- Add a **discriminating regression test** that distinguishes `main` vs this PR behavior.

## Motivation
- Related issue: #499
- Current InsertSync is conservative for some sibling-subview patterns and may insert redundant `PIPE_V` barrier.
- This PR applies a temporary, policy-based assumption (easy to revert in one commit) while keeping parent-child safety unchanged.

## Design
- File: `lib/PTO/Transforms/InsertSync/MemoryDependentAnalyzer.cpp`
- In local-memory `MemAlias`:
  - identify tile subview values via `pto.bind_tile` with `pto.view_semantics="subview"`, peeling to `memref.subview`
  - if both values are sibling subviews from the same parent source, return no-alias
  - otherwise keep existing logic unchanged

## Testing
- Build:
  - `ninja -C build ptoas`

- New guard (discriminating):
  - `test/basic/issue499_subview_sibling_dynamic_offset_nonoverlap_regression.pto`
  - A/B verification:
    - `main`: generated code contains `pipe_barrier(PIPE_V)`
    - this PR: generated code does **not** contain `pipe_barrier(PIPE_V)`

- Existing guard (non-discriminating baseline):
  - `test/basic/issue499_subview_sibling_nonoverlap_assumption_regression.pto`

- Regression guards:
  - `test/lit/pto/issue428_cube_sync_regression.pto`
  - `test/lit/pto/issue454_nested_loop_same_pipe_pair_regression.pto`
  - `test/lit/pto/issue454_loop_if_else_loop_carried_sync_regression.pto`

## Risk
- This is a policy-based assumption and depends on upper-layer contract correctness.
- If upper layer violates sibling-subview non-overlap, wrong sync elimination is possible.

## Rollback
- Revert this PR (single-topic change, isolated and easy to roll back).

title: [Bug] tprelu triggers vec overflow on A5
body:
### Component

### Description

`pto.tprelu` can trigger `vec overflow` on `main` with a single-file minimal PTO repro.

title: [Feature] Move plan memory / insert sync from memref world to tile_buf world
body:
Suggested label: `enhancement`

## Summary

当前 PTOAS pipeline 将 `plan memory` 和 `insert sync` 放在 `View2Memref` 之后执行：

```text
[tile_buf world]
  (op fusion plan -> gen fusion region -> ...)
-> View2Memref
-> [memref world]
  (plan memory -> insert sync -> expand tileop -> ...)
```

这个 pass 边界在早期帮助我们复用 memref-world 的实现，但现在已经开始限制 tile-level 能力演进。我们希望将 `plan memory`、`insert sync` 以及与之强相关的大部分中高层 pass 前移到 `tile_buf world`，把 `View2Memref` 明确收敛为高层 Tile IR 到低层 memref IR 的边界。

目标 pipeline 形态：

```text
[tile_buf world]
  (plan memory -> insert sync -> op fusion -> expand tileop)
-> View2Memref
-> [memref world]
  (low level optimizations -> backend lowering -> ...)
```

这不是单纯的 pass 重排，而是为了让同步、融合和 TileOp 展开都发生在语义最完整的表示层上。

## Motivation / use case

### 1. 当前 pass 边界直接阻塞更高等级的 op fusion

我们希望在 `tile_buf world` 做 op fusion，因为这个阶段保留了最完整的 tile 语义信息，包括：

- tile 的布局和 config
- valid shape
- tile-level producer / consumer 关系
- 更贴近上层语义的 alias / buffer 使用形态

但 `level 3` 的 op fusion 实际上依赖 `insert sync` 的结果，因为融合不能跨越 sync point。当前 `insert sync` 位于 `memref world`，意味着 `tile_buf world` 在做融合决策时看不到最终同步边界，只能停留在不依赖 sync 结果的 `level 2` fusion。

换句话说，现有 pipeline 的问题不是“还没实现 level 3 fusion”，而是“当前 IR 分层方式让 level 3 fusion 无法在正确的位置实现”。

### 2. 当前 pipeline 让 `expand tileop` 之前发生了一次不必要的类型世界往返

`ExpandTileOp` 的模板函数接口本身就是 `Tile` / `tile_buf`。仓库里的 pass 描述也已经明确：

- `ExpandTileOp` 生成的模板函数使用 `tile_buf` 参数
- `MemrefToTileBuf` 的存在，是为了在 `PTOViewToMemref + PlanMemory + InsertSync` 之后重新恢复 `tile_buf` 语义，再继续做 Tile-level lowering

这意味着当前 pipeline 实际上在 `expand tileop` 前经历了：

```text
tile_buf -> View2Memref -> memref -> MemrefToTileBuf -> tile_buf
```

这条链路带来几个问题：

- 需要额外维护一条 `memref -> tile_buf` 的恢复路径，只是为了回到 TileOp lib 所需的接口形态
- 中间经过一次语义降级后再恢复，增加了类型、metadata、anchor 和 verifier 一致性的维护成本
- 新增 TileOp / TileBuf 能力时，需要同时考虑 lowering 和 recovery 两侧，增加系统脆弱性

如果 `plan memory` / `insert sync` 本来就是中高层语义 pass，那么让它们停留在 `tile_buf world`，可以避免这次“先降级再恢复”的往返。

### 3. 现在的分层方式已经开始影响 PTOAS 的功能完备性和稳定性

上述两个问题并不是孤立的工程不便，而是在持续影响 PTOAS 的能力边界：

- 功能完备性：sync-aware fusion、更多 tile-level 优化和更自然的 TileOp 展开都会受到限制
- 稳定性：额外的 IR world 往返意味着更多 bridge、更多隐式约束和更多恢复失败的可能性

随着 tile-level 功能继续扩展，把中高层 pass 长期放在 `memref world` 的成本只会越来越高。

## Proposed API / behavior

建议将 `tile_buf world` 和 `memref world` 的职责边界重新定义为：

- `tile_buf world`：负责高层语义相关的 memory planning、sync insertion、fusion、tileop expansion
- `memref world`：负责低层 canonicalization、backend-oriented optimization 和最终 lowering

具体上，希望逐步达成以下结果：

1. `plan memory` 在 `tile_buf world` 上工作，直接消费 Tile-level buffer / alias 信息，而不是等到 `View2Memref` 之后再规划。
2. `insert sync` 在 `tile_buf world` 上工作，使 sync point 成为 fusion 和后续高层优化可见的边界。
3. `op fusion` 在拿到 sync 信息后执行，能够支持真正受 sync point 约束的更高等级融合。
4. `expand tileop` 直接在 `tile_buf world` 完成，避免为了调用 TileOp lib 再从 memref 恢复回 `tile_buf`。
5. `View2Memref` 作为更清晰的阶段边界，只承接已经完成高层决策的 Tile IR。

如果一次性迁移过大，也可以接受分阶段演进，但最终目标应当是让 `MemrefToTileBuf` 不再承担“为高层 pass 回补语义”的核心职责。

## Additional context

仓库里已经存在一些信号，说明当前 pass 分层正在承受额外复杂度：

- `ExpandTileOp` 的描述明确指出模板函数使用 `tile_buf` 参数，并直接以 `tile_buf` 作为调用接口
- `MemrefToTileBuf` 的描述明确指出它是在 `PTOViewToMemref + PlanMemory + InsertSync` 之后恢复 `tile_buf`，以便后续 Tile->Vector lowering 继续基于 tile_buf 语义工作
- `PTOViewToMemref` 还需要专门插入 `pto.bind_tile` 作为锚点，供后续恢复 tile_buf 类型使用

这些都说明当前 pipeline 已经不是“自然地在 memref world 完成后续流程”，而是“先降到 memref world，再想办法恢复出高层 Tile 语义继续工作”。

建议把这个 issue 作为 pipeline 分层调整的总入口，后续再拆分出更细的 implementation issue，例如：

- tile_buf-world memory planning 的表示和地址回填方式
- tile_buf-world sync analysis / sync insertion
- sync-aware level 3 fusion
- `ExpandTileOp` 前移后的 pipeline 收敛
- `MemrefToTileBuf` 的降级、收缩或移除

title: [Bug] auto-sync should track aliasing through `pto.subview`
body:
### Component

PTO Dialect / ODS (include/PTO/IR)

### Description

The auto-sync pass treats the result of `pto.subset` as an independent
buffer rather than an alias of its source tile. As a consequence, no
sync flag (`set_flag` / `wait_flag` pair) is emitted between a write
to a sub-view and a later read/write of either the parent tile or an
overlapping sub-view. Kernels that use `pto.subset` to express
sub-block parallelism (each AIV sub-block owning a row-half of a
shared tile) produce wrong data.

### Reproduction (minimal)

```mlir
module {
  func.func @cube_kernel(%arg0: !pto.ptr<f32>, %arg1: !pto.ptr<f16>, %arg2: !pto.ptr<f16>, %arg3: !pto.ptr<f16>) attributes {pto.kernel_kind = #pto.kernel_kind<cube>} {
    %c0 = arith.constant 0 : index
    %c1 = arith.constant 1 : index
    %c32 = arith.constant 32 : index
    %c32_0 = arith.constant 32 : index
    %c256 = arith.constant 256 : index
    %c8192 = arith.constant 8192 : index
    %c32_1 = arith.constant 32 : index
    %c64 = arith.constant 64 : index
    %0 = pto.get_block_num
    %1 = arith.index_cast %0 : i64 to index
    %2 = pto.get_block_idx
    %3 = arith.index_cast %2 : i64 to index
```

Vector kernel pattern (simplified):

```python
sb_idx     = pto.get_subblock_idx()
row_off_sb = sb_idx * S0_HALF                       # 0 or 16

# Shared full-size tile, allocated once per func
p_fp16 = pto.alloc_tile(p_fp16_ty)                  # [S0=32, S1_TILE]

# Each sub-block grabs its own non-overlapping row-half
p_fp16_half = pto.subset(
    p_fp16,
    offsets=[row_off_sb, 0],
    sizes=[S0_HALF, S1_TILE],
)

# ... softmax compute writing into `p_fp16_half` ...
tile.cvt(p_fp32_half, p_fp16_half)                  # WRITE via subset

# Later: collective op reads the parent tile
pto.tpush_to_aic(p_fp16, 0)                         # READ of parent
```

The RAW dependency from `tile.cvt(... p_fp16_half)` to
`pto.tpush_to_aic(p_fp16, 0)` is invisible to the auto-sync pass
because `p_fp16_half` and `p_fp16` are distinct SSA values. No flag is
emitted; the push reads stale data.

Manual `pto.pipe_barrier("V")` calls inserted at every cross-sub-block
seam reduce but do not eliminate the mismatch (because they only order
within a sub-block, not across).

## Diagnostic

To isolate the alias-tracking issue from the orthogonal "pipe ops
under sub-block parallelism" question (separate issue), I ran the
following control:

- Force both sub-blocks to compute the **upper** 16-row half
  (`row_off_sb = 0` for both).
- Only sub-block 0 commits the GM store.
- Lower 16 rows of every output block are intentionally untouched
  (≈ 50% of elements baseline-wrong).

Result: **47.8% mismatch** — i.e. less than the 50% baseline, meaning
the upper 16 rows are computed correctly. So:

- The half-view algorithm and the `pto.subset` op itself are correct.
- When both sub-blocks are also active and writing to non-overlapping
  halves of the same parent (the realistic case), mismatch jumps to
  ~64% — the cross-sub-block writes are not getting the WAR/RAW
  protection auto-sync would normally insert for the parent.

### Expected behavior

Two ops `A`, `B` accessing memory through any of:
- the parent tile `t`,
- `subset(t, ...)` or any chain of subsets rooted at `t`,

should be treated by the auto-sync dependency tracker as touching the
same memory. Standard 'set_flag / wait_flag' analysis on the parent tile. If the
subsets can be proven non-overlapping at compile time (constant
offsets + sizes), the pass may skip emitting a flag for that pair as
an optimisation.

### Actual behavior / error logs

Result: **47.8% mismatch** against torch npu reference — i.e. less than the 50% baseline, meaning the upper 16 rows are computed correctly. So:

- The half-view algorithm and the `pto.subset` op itself are correct.
- When both sub-blocks are also active and writing to non-overlapping
  halves of the same parent (the realistic case), mismatch jumps to
  ~64% — the cross-sub-block writes are not getting the WAR/RAW
  protection auto-sync would normally insert for the parent.

title: refactor: drop integer signedness checks in PTO verifiers
body:
## 问题背景
- PTO IR 文档中的多处算子约束使用“支持 i8/i16/i32”等位宽描述，而非区分 signless/unsigned。
- `lib/PTO/IR/PTO.cpp` 的多个 verifier 仍显式使用 `isSignless/isUnsigned/isUnsignedInteger/isSignlessInteger` 做符号语义校验，导致与“按位宽支持”口径不一致。

## 定位分析
- 在 `PTO.cpp` 中，符号相关校验分布在通用类型辅助函数和多个 op verifier（如 tstore/tquant/tdequant/tsort32/thistogram/tmovfp/tstorefp、row/col arg reduce 等）。
- 这些校验的共同模式是：先判断位宽，再附加 signedness 约束；其中一部分 lit 用例（tquant wrong dst）也依赖该旧行为。

## 解决方案
- 将上述 verifier 中的整数校验统一改为“仅检查位宽”，去除 signedness 条件：
  - 去掉 `isSignless/isUnsigned/isUnsignedInteger/isSignlessInteger` 的验证分支；
  - 保留原有位宽/形状/布局/地址空间等约束。
- 同步更新受影响回归用例：
  - `test/lit/pto/tquant_verify_invalid_int8_sym_wrong_dst.pto`
  - `test/lit/pto/tquant_verify_invalid_int8_asym_wrong_dst.pto`

## Summary
- route A3 remote validation through `task-submit` instead of running NPU jobs directly over SSH
- default the workflow's `device_id` input to `auto` so the queue picks an allowed device
- map `TASK_DEVICE` back into `DEVICE_ID` before invoking `run_remote_npu_validation.sh`

## Why
The A3 host at `101.245.68.6` now exposes NPU access through `task-submit` rather than direct `/dev/davinci*` access for `zhongxuan`.

I verified on the host that:
- `zhongxuan` can still SSH in
- direct login only has groups `zhongxuan,wheel`
- `/dev/davinci*` is owned by `HwHiAiUser`
- `task-submit --device auto --run ...` switches the task into `HwHiAiUser` and exposes `TASK_DEVICE`
- the exact `ssh -> task-submit -> bash ./test/npu_validation/scripts/run_remote_npu_validation.sh` command shape used here correctly propagates `DEVICE_ID`

## Validation
- `python3` YAML parse of `.github/workflows/ci.yml`
- live probe on `101.245.68.6` using the workflow-equivalent `task-submit` wrapper:
  - `DEVICE_ID` resolved to the allocated card
  - `TASK_DEVICE` matched it
  - the wrapped script ran as `HwHiAiUser`

title: [InsertSync] fix zero-trip loop sync merge (issue #533)
body:
Summary
- Fix InsertSync loop-state merge to be zero-trip safe by default (no new option).
- Add regression test for issue #533 reproducer.

Motivation
- Fixes #533.
- Existing logic in `InsertLoopSync` unconditionally promoted loop-body `alreadySync` into outer state, which is unsound when loop may execute zero iterations.

Design
- In `InsertLoopSync`, do not promote `alreadySync` from loop-body traversal.
- Keep only `syncFinder` updates from loop-body traversal, consistent with no-else branch handling in `InsertBranchSync`.
- This preserves correctness for both zero-trip and non-zero-trip executions under default behavior.

Testing
- Reproduced issue #533 from provided `.pto` input.
- Before fix: missing post-loop `wait_flag(PIPE_MTE2, PIPE_V, ...)` before `TROWEXPANDDIV`.
- After fix: `wait_flag(PIPE_MTE2, PIPE_V, EVENT_ID2)` appears before `TROWEXPANDDIV`.
- Added lit regression: `test/lit/pto/issue533_loop_zero_trip_sync_regression.pto`.
- Ran local checks:
  - `ptoas test/lit/pto/issue533_loop_zero_trip_sync_regression.pto --pto-arch=a3 --pto-level=level3 --enable-insert-sync | FileCheck ...`
  - `ptoas test/lit/pto/issue454_loop_if_else_loop_carried_sync_regression.pto --pto-arch=a3 --enable-insert-sync | FileCheck ...`
  - `ptoas test/lit/pto/issue454_nested_loop_same_pipe_pair_regression.pto --pto-arch=a3 --enable-insert-sync | FileCheck ...`

Risk / Rollback
- Risk: potential extra syncs for some loop patterns due to conservative merge.
- Rollback: revert this PR commit if needed.

title: [Bug] Non-deterministic UB allocator: identical MLIR input produces different `.cpp` outputs across runs, some of which compute incorrect results
body:
### Component

PTO Dialect / ODS (include/PTO/IR)

### Description

Running `ptoas` repeatedly on a **byte-identical** input `.pto` file produces **different `.cpp` outputs** on each invocation. The differences are not cosmetic: the UB tile base addresses (`pto.pointer_cast(%cN_i64)`) get reshuffled, and some of the resulting layouts compute **numerically wrong results** at runtime — i.e. on those layouts two logically-distinct tiles end up sharing overlapping lifetimes/storage and stomp on each other.

Concretely, on our Sinkhorn kernel:

- `md5sum sinkhorn.pto` is stable (same bytes every time the Python builder runs).
- `md5sum` of `ptoas`'s output `.cpp` differs across consecutive invocations.
- The `.so` built from the "lucky" layout passes 66/66 correctness cases at `rtol=2e-3, atol=1e-3`.
- The `.so` built from an "unlucky" layout fails 12/66 cases at the same tolerance, and **still fails 17/66 cases at the very loose `rtol=5e-2, atol=1e-2`** (so this is real wrong-arithmetic, not a precision regression).

The failures are concentrated on specific dynamic shapes (`N=4, K=32, L=64` and `N=4, K=64, L=32` for our kernel), this is consistent with an allocator-aliasing bug whose manifestation depends on which loop iteration first happens to write to the colliding tile.

This makes builds non-reproducible and silently miscompiled.

### Reproduction (minimal)

The `.pto` is generated by the PTODSL Sinkhorn builder in https://github.com/huawei-csl/pto-dsl/pull/117:

- Builder: `examples/aot/sinkhorn_dynamic_multicore/sinkhorn_builder.py`
- Generated IR (attached below): `sinkhorn.pto`

```bash
cd /mounted_home/pto-dsl/examples/aot/sinkhorn_dynamic_multicore

# 1. Confirm the input .pto is deterministic.
python3 sinkhorn_builder.py > /tmp/a.pto
python3 sinkhorn_builder.py > /tmp/b.pto
md5sum /tmp/a.pto /tmp/b.pto
#   5117399319df1c521c3fe0ee9f750e99  /tmp/a.pto
#   5117399319df1c521c3fe0ee9f750e99  /tmp/b.pto       <-- IDENTICAL

# 2. Run ptoas three times on the *same* input.
for i in 1 2 3; do
    ptoas --enable-insert-sync /tmp/a.pto -o /tmp/r$i.cpp
    md5sum /tmp/r$i.cpp
done
# Observed:
#   f4c0d4a6d4e654a9f0fe8b57f8735ce0  /tmp/r1.cpp
#   330760db3d1d225daadf92967cfc0b6e  /tmp/r2.cpp
#   dfe9db622c2d46caf0563c572cd6a233  /tmp/r3.cpp     <-- ALL DIFFERENT
```

Diffing the outputs shows the divergence is in the UB pointer-cast constants emitted at the top of the kernel, e.g.:

```bash
-  const int64_t v28 = 15392;
-  const int64_t v29 = 16416;
-  const int64_t v30 = 25632;
+  const int64_t v28 = 1024;
+  const int64_t v29 = 29888;
+  const int64_t v30 = 3104;
   ...
```

To observe the **functional** consequence (one layout correct, another broken), build twice and run the correctness tests:

```bash
bash compile.sh                                         # bad layout (example)
python ./run_sinkhorn.py --lib ./sinkhorn_lib.so --rtol 2e-3 --atol 1e-3
#   totals: {'match': 54, 'mismatch': 12, 'skip': 0}
```
```bash
bash compile.sh                                         # try again — sometimes good, sometimes bad
python ./run_sinkhorn.py --lib ./sinkhorn_lib.so --rtol 2e-3 --atol 1e-3
#   totals: {'match': 66, 'mismatch':  0, 'skip': 0}
```

The 12 failing cases are always the same shapes: every (order, seed) combination of `(N=4, K=32, L=64)` and `(N=4, K=64, L=32)`.

The MLIR is always the same:

```mlir

  func.func @_kernel(%arg0: !pto.ptr<f16>, %arg1: !pto.ptr<f16>, %arg2: !pto.ptr<f16>, %arg3: !pto.ptr<f16>, %arg4: i32, %arg5: i32, %arg6: i32, %arg7: i32, %arg8: f32, %arg9: f32, %arg10: f32, %arg11: f32, %arg12: f32, %arg13: f32) {

            pto.tmuls ins(%54, %cst_0 : !pto.tile_buf<vec, 1x8xf32>, f32) outs(%37 : !pto.tile_buf<vec, 1x8xf32>)
            %55 = pto.treshape %37 : !pto.tile_buf<vec, 1x8xf32> -> !pto.tile_buf<vec, 8x1xf32, blayout=col_major>
            pto.trowexpanddiv ins(%33, %55 : !pto.tile_buf<vec, 8x256xf32, valid=8x?>, !pto.tile_buf<vec, 8x1xf32, blayout=col_major>) outs(%33 : !pto.tile_buf<vec, 8x256xf32, valid=8x?>)
            pto.tcolexpandmul ins(%33, %25 : !pto.tile_buf<vec, 8x256xf32, valid=8x?>, !pto.tile_buf<vec, 1x256xf32, valid=1x?>) outs(%33 : !pto.tile_buf<vec, 8x256xf32, valid=8x?>)
            pto.tcvt ins(%33 {rmode = #pto<round_mode CAST_RINT>} : !pto.tile_buf<vec, 8x256xf32, valid=8x?>) outs(%32 : !pto.tile_buf<vec, 8x256xf16, valid=8x?>)
            %56 = arith.addi %48, %arg15 : index
            %57 = pto.partition_view %45, offsets = [%56, %c0], sizes = [%c8, %2] : !pto.tensor_view<?x?xf16> -> !pto.partition_tensor_view<8x256xf16>
            pto.tstore ins(%32 : !pto.tile_buf<vec, 8x256xf16, valid=8x?>) outs(%57 : !pto.partition_tensor_view<8x256xf16>)
          }
          pto.tcvt ins(%23 {rmode = #pto<round_mode CAST_RINT>} : !pto.tile_buf<vec, 1x256xf32, valid=1x?>) outs(%41 : !pto.tile_buf<vec, 1x256xf16, valid=1x?>)
          %50 = pto.partition_view %46, offsets = [%arg14, %c0], sizes = [%c1, %2] : !pto.tensor_view<?x?xf16> -> !pto.partition_tensor_view<1x256xf16>
          pto.tstore ins(%41 : !pto.tile_buf<vec, 1x256xf16, valid=1x?>) outs(%50 : !pto.partition_tensor_view<1x256xf16>)
          pto.tcvt ins(%24 {rmode = #pto<round_mode CAST_RINT>} : !pto.tile_buf<vec, 1x256xf32, valid=1x?>) outs(%42 : !pto.tile_buf<vec, 1x256xf16, valid=1x?>)
          %51 = pto.partition_view %47, offsets = [%arg14, %c0], sizes = [%c1, %1] : !pto.tensor_view<?x?xf16> -> !pto.partition_tensor_view<1x256xf16>
          pto.tstore ins(%42 : !pto.tile_buf<vec, 1x256xf16, valid=1x?>) outs(%51 : !pto.partition_tensor_view<1x256xf16>)
        }
      }
    }
    return
  }
}
```

title: fix: avoid false A5 tprelu vec overflow
body:
## 问题背景
- issue #531 反馈：A5 下 `pto.tprelu` 在 `256x200` 最小复现用例会报 `vec overflow`，而该场景不应因为 `tmp` 触发额外本地内存压力。
- 现象在 `hw/main` 上可稳定复现，错误为 `requires 2048000 bits while 2031616 bits avaliable`。

## 定位分析
- 内存规划 pass 会将 PTO_DPS op 中“被标记为 write 且不是 dps init 的 operand”当作 scratch buffer 纳入本地内存规划。
- `TPReluOp::getEffects` 之前对所有架构都声明 `tmp` 为 write，因此 A5 也会把 `tmp` 计入 vec 内存峰值，导致与 `dst` 叠加后触发假性 overflow。
- 对照 A5 pto-isa `TPrelu.hpp`，A5 `TPRELU_IMPL` 并不实际使用 `tmp`，因此该写入建模在 A5 上是过度约束。

## 解决方案
- 修改 `lib/PTO/IR/PTO.cpp`：在 `TPReluOp::getEffects` 中按架构区分，A5 不再将 `tmp` 声明为 write effect（A2/A3 保持不变）。
- 新增回归测试 `test/lit/pto/issue531_tprelu_vec_overflow_a5.pto`，覆盖 issue 复现形状并断言 A5 编译不再出现 `vec overflow`。
- 验证：
  - `./build/tools/ptoas/ptoas --pto-arch=a5 issue531_repro.pto -o -`（复现用例转为通过）
  - `cmake --build build --target check-pto -j8`（120/120 通过）

title: [Bug] ptoas silently produces a hanging kernel when a tile's valid_row/valid_col is negative at runtime
body:
### Component

Verifier / IR semantics (lib/PTO/IR)

### Description

When an input `.pto` program has a tile whose dynamic `valid_row` / `valid_col` can evaluate to a **negative** value at runtime (for example, `minsi(A - k, C)` where `k > A`), `ptoas` happily generates a kernel that issues `TLOAD`/`TMOV`/`TMATMUL` with that negative valid dim. On the hardware the malformed DMA lands the pipe event scoreboard in an unrecoverable state and the kernel hangs forever — no error, no fault, no log.

The invariant `valid_row >= 0` and `valid_col >= 0` is part of the implicit contract of `pto.alloc_tile` / `pto.tload` etc., but it is nowhere enforced — neither at IR verification time, nor by a runtime guard in the generated kernel. A user who accidentally emits an overshooting driver loop (e.g. `for n in range(0, 8192 + 383, 384)` which produces `n = 8448 > 8192`) has no visible signal that anything is wrong; the only symptom is "kernel 16 never returns."

Related: #322 (verifier should reject shape mismatches on TStore), #533 (missing sync when loop zero-iterates). These all fall under the broader theme of "ptoas accepts malformed tile sizes and emits code that breaks at runtime."

### Reproduction (minimal)

Submit to `ptoas` any kernel where the allocated tile's valid dim can be negative — the pattern in real code looks like this (trimmed from a qwen3 decode kernel):

```mlir
%c8192_index  = arith.constant 8192 : index
%c384_index   = arith.constant 384  : index

// arg3 is the external loop's `n` — caller passes n = 8448 on the last iter
func.func @k(..., %arg3: index) {
  %diff  = arith.subi %c8192_index, %arg3 : index         // 8192 - 8448 = -256
  %vcol  = arith.minsi %diff, %c384_index : index         // min(-256, 384) = -256
  %tile  = pto.alloc_tile ... valid_col = %vcol
          : !pto.tile_buf<loc=mat, dtype=bf16, rows=64, cols=384, v_row=64, v_col=?, ...>
  %part  = pto.partition_view ...
  pto.tload ins(%part) outs(%tile)
  // ...tmov, tmatmul on the same tile
}
```

Compile:

```bash
ptoas input.pto -o out.cpp
```

A full reproducible case is the `Qwen3Decode` kernel 16 generated at pypto commit `103aaa94` — dump in `build_output/Qwen3Decode_20260422_122654/ptoas/qwen3_decode_incore_16.pto`, emitted kernel in the same directory's `.cpp`. Caller at `orchestration/qwen3_decode.cpp:375` passes `n = 8448` on the 23rd iteration.

### Expected behavior

Either:

1. **Compile-time** — `ptoas` does a value-range check on `valid_row`/`valid_col` operands and errors out if it can statically prove the value can be negative (e.g. `minsi(sub(const_A, x), const_C)` with no lower bound on `x`). At minimum, warn.
2. **Runtime** — generated kernel emits a guard such as
   ```cpp
   if ((int32_t)valid_col < 0 || (int32_t)valid_row < 0) {
       // either: early return (treat as no-op)
       // or:     trap / write error code + return
   }
   ```
   placed before any `TLOAD`/`TMOV`/`TMATMUL` that uses the tile. Silent hang is the worst possible failure mode.

Option 2 is strictly more actionable for users since it surfaces the bug at the first bad iteration rather than requiring the user to diff against a known-good version. Option 1 is a "nice to have" that catches a subset of cases earlier.

### Actual behavior / error logs

```text
ptoas exits 0, emits a kernel that contains e.g.:

  int32_t v31 = (int32_t)((uint32_t)v12 - (uint32_t)v4);   // 8192 - 8448 wraps: v31 = -256
  int32_t v32 = v31 < v11 ? v31 : v11;                     // v32 = -256
  Tile<..., -1, -1, ...> v33 = Tile<..., -1, -1, ...>(v23, v32);
  ...
  TLOAD(v34, v39);   // negative valid_col
  TMOV (v68, v34);
  TMATMUL_ACC(...); // hangs here / on the matching set_flag / wait_flag

Host-side: runtime sits waiting on kernel completion signal; no error reported.
```

### Git commit

`ptoas 0.26` (binary release; no source tree available on this machine — please treat this as "reproduces on 0.26" and verify against current tip).

Linux (aarch64)

### Target Ascend arch (if relevant)

a3

title: [PlanMemory] Stabilize ordering and reject overlapping UB layouts
body:
## Summary
- stabilize PlanMemory buffer ordering in scratch/gen/kill/liveness paths with a stable value key
- reject planned UB layouts that still overlap across temporally live or semantically conflicting tiles
- remove iteration-order dependence so recompiling the same input no longer picks different valid layouts

## Why
Issue #541 exposed that PlanMemory could depend on unstable container iteration order. The allocator must be functionally correct for every dynamic shape that satisfies the kernel's `scf.if` guard, with no aliasing between tiles whose lifetimes overlap. This change makes the planner deterministic and adds a post-plan overlap check so invalid layouts fail fast instead of silently compiling.

Refs #541.

## Validation
- recompiled the issue #541 `.pto` twice with the modified `ptoas`; generated C++ md5 stayed `398678d906bd1f94c297179a36a178da`
- the corresponding compile logs also matched across runs; md5 stayed `7e5786a610fec5d27de7b0009377e0fd`
- verified the PR diff contains only `lib/PTO/Transforms/PTOPlanMemory.cpp`

title: [Bug] Unclear error when ptoas lowers pto.tfillpad with mismatched src/dst tile types
body:
### Component

EmitC / Codegen (lib/PTO/Transforms/PTOToEmitC.cpp)

### Description

When `ptoas` lowers a `pto.tfillpad` whose source and destination tiles differ in `v_row`/`v_col` (dynamic vs. static) **and** in `pad` (null vs. zero), it emits C++ with two `Tile<…>` declarations that have incompatible template parameter lists. The pto-isa `TFILLPAD` library has no `Mat` overload that accepts this combination, so compilation fails deep in the C++ toolchain with a diagnostic that elides the crucial template arguments (`[5 * …]`, `[2 * …]`, `[…]`) and never mentions which tile field mismatches.

The user is left with four lines of `no matching function for call to 'TFILLPAD'` and no actionable information. There is no MLIR-level error, no source-location context, and the clang-rendered type tags hide the exact template parameters that differ.

The underlying problem is a type-unification gap in EmitC (or a missing verifier check on `pto.tfillpad`). The *reporting* problem is that the user discovers the gap only after attempting to compile the generated C++.

### Reproduction (minimal)

Input MLIR (as produced by pypto, `build_output/<run>/ptoas/qwen3_decode_incore_16.pto:38`):

```mlir
pto.tfillpad
  ins(%src  : !pto.tile_buf<loc=mat, dtype=bf16, rows=16, cols=64,
                            v_row=?,  v_col=?,  blayout=col_major,
                            slayout=row_major, fractal=512, pad=0>)
  outs(%dst : !pto.tile_buf<loc=mat, dtype=bf16, rows=16, cols=64,
                            v_row=16, v_col=64, blayout=col_major,
                            slayout=row_major, fractal=512, pad=1>)
```

Command:

```bash
ptoas qwen3_decode_incore_16.pto -o qwen3_decode_incore_16.cpp
# …then the usual C++ build step over the emitted file.
```

Four `pto.tfillpad` sites in the same file reproduce the same failure (with the `rows=64, cols=384` variant also present).

### Expected behavior

`ptoas` should either:

1. **Reject the op in the MLIR verifier** with a diagnostic naming the mismatched fields, e.g.

   ```
   error: 'pto.tfillpad' operand/result tile types are not lowerable to a
   pto-isa TFILLPAD overload:
     src  !pto.tile_buf<..., v_row=?,  v_col=?,  pad=null>
     dst  !pto.tile_buf<..., v_row=16, v_col=64, pad=zero>
   Mismatching fields: v_row (?  vs 16), v_col (?  vs 64), pad (null vs zero).
   Note: pto-isa only exposes a heterogeneous TFILLPAD overload for loc=vec.
   ```

2. **Or normalise the types in EmitC** before emitting so src and dst share the same `Tile<…>` specialization (e.g. declare both with `v_row=?, v_col=?, pad=null` and use `set_validshape` + the single-operand `TFILLPAD_INPLACE` form).

Either fix also solves the reporting problem: the user never sees the opaque clang diagnostic.

### Actual behavior / error logs

Generated C++ (`qwen3_decode_incore_16.cpp:139`):

```cpp
// v23 — source
Tile<TileType::Mat, bfloat16_t, 16, 64, BLayout::ColMajor,
     -1, -1,
     SLayout::RowMajor, 512, PadValue::Null, CompactMode::Null> v23 = ...;
TLOAD(v23, ...);

// v51 — destination
Tile<TileType::Mat, bfloat16_t, 16, 64, BLayout::ColMajor,
     16, 64,
     SLayout::RowMajor, 512, PadValue::Zero, CompactMode::Null> v51;
TFILLPAD(v51, v23);   // <-- no matching function
```

Template parameters that differ between `dst` (v51) and `src` (v23):

| Position | Param | dst (v51) | src (v23) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6 | valid block rows | `16` | `-1` |
| 7 | valid block cols | `64` | `-1` |
| 10 | `PadValue` | `Zero` | `Null` |

pto-isa provides only two `TFILLPAD` overloads (`pto/common/pto_instr.hpp`):

- **Homogeneous** (line 885): `TFILLPAD(TileData& dst, TileData& src, …)` — deduction fails because `dst` and `src` resolve to different `Tile<…>` specializations.
- **Heterogeneous** (line 895): `TFILLPAD(DstTileData& dst, SrcTileData& src, …)` — constrained by `requires Loc == TileType::Vec`. Both tiles here are `loc=mat`, so SFINAE rejects it.

Raw clang output (trimmed, note the elided fields — this is all the user sees):

```
.../qwen3_decode_incore_16.cpp:139:5: error: no matching function for call to 'TFILLPAD'
    TFILLPAD(v51, v23);
    ^~~~~~~~
.../pto/common/pto_instr.hpp:885:22: note: candidate template ignored:
  deduced conflicting types for parameter 'TileData'
  ('Tile<[5 * ...], 16, 64, [2 * ...], PadValue::Zero aka 1, [...]>' vs.
   'Tile<[5 * ...], -1, -1, [2 * ...], PadValue::Null aka 0, [...]>')
PTO_INST RecordEvent TFILLPAD(TileData &dst, TileData &src, WaitEvents &... events)
                     ^
.../pto/common/pto_instr.hpp:895:22: note: candidate template ignored:
  requirement '(…::Loc == TileType::Vec) && (…::Loc == TileType::Vec)' was not satisfied
PTO_INST RecordEvent TFILLPAD(DstTileData &dst, SrcTileData &src, WaitEvents &... events)
                     ^
[ERROR] … ERR99999 UNKNOWN applicaiton exception
```

Nothing in this output tells the user that the mismatch is in `v_row`/`v_col`/`pad`; the rest of the template parameters are elided and the source MLIR location is lost.

title: fix: refactor duplicated code
fix: preserve unsigned scalar type in TCI emitc lowering
body:
**问题背景**
pto.tci 的 ui32 输入被降到了 TCI<..., int32_t, ...>，unsigned 语义丢失。

**定位分析**
输入 .pto 中 ins 是 ui32，前端类型没问题。
问题出在 EmitC lowering：PTOTCIToEmitC 里模板参数 scalarTok 只按位宽映射为 int16_t/int32_t，没有区分 signed/unsigned。
因此 ui32 也被错误写成了 int32_t 模板参数。

**解决方法**
修改 lib/PTO/Transforms/PTOToEmitC.cpp：在 PTOTCIToEmitC 中按 IntegerType 的 signed/unsigned + 位宽选择模板类型：
ui16 -> uint16_t
ui32 -> uint32_t
i16/i32 保持原样

title: [Feature] Add indexed tconcat form matching A5 C++ TCONCAT_IMPL(dst, src0, src1, src0Idx, src1Idx)
body:
### Summary

`hw-native-sys/PTOAS` currently exposes `pto.tconcat` only as the plain 3-operand tile concatenate form:

```mlir
pto.tconcat ins(%src0, %src1 : !pto.tile_buf<...>, !pto.tile_buf<...>)
           outs(%dst : !pto.tile_buf<...>)
```

However, the A5 C++ PTO ISA also provides an **indexed concat** form that takes two extra index tiles:

```cpp
template <typename TileDst, typename TileSrc0, typename TileSrc1, typename TileSrc0Idx, typename TileSrc1Idx>
PTO_INTERNAL void TCONCAT_IMPL(TileDst &dst, TileSrc0 &src0, TileSrc1 &src1, TileSrc0Idx &src0Idx, TileSrc1Idx &src1Idx)
```

This indexed form is currently missing from the official PTO dialect / PTOAS frontend surface.

### Motivation / use case

Some A5 kernels need to concatenate values from `src0` and `src1` into `dst` according to two per-source index tiles rather than by simple contiguous column append.

The corresponding C++ implementation is already defined through:

```cpp
template <typename TileDst, typename TileSrc0, typename TileSrc1, typename TileSrc0Idx, typename TileSrc1Idx>
PTO_INTERNAL void TCONCAT_IMPL(TileDst &dst, TileSrc0 &src0, TileSrc1 &src1, TileSrc0Idx &src0Idx, TileSrc1Idx &src1Idx)
{
    using dataType = typename TileDst::DType;
    using idxType = typename TileSrc0Idx::DType;

    static_assert(std::is_same<dataType, typename TileSrc0::DType>::value &&
                      std::is_same<dataType, typename TileSrc0::DType>::value,
                  "TCONCAT: Data type of dst, src0 and src1 must be the same.");
    static_assert(std::is_same<idxType, typename TileSrc1Idx::DType>::value,
                  "TCONCAT: Data type of src0Idx and src1Idx must be the same.");
    static_assert(std::is_same<dataType, int32_t>::value || std::is_same<dataType, int16_t>::value ||
                      std::is_same<dataType, int8_t>::value || std::is_same<dataType, uint32_t>::value ||
                      std::is_same<dataType, uint16_t>::value || std::is_same<dataType, uint8_t>::value ||
                      std::is_same<dataType, half>::value || std::is_same<dataType, float32_t>::value ||
                      std::is_same<dataType, bfloat16_t>::value,
                  "TCONCAT: Invalid data type.");
    static_assert(TileDst::Loc == TileType::Vec && TileSrc0::Loc == TileType::Vec && TileSrc1::Loc == TileType::Vec,
                  "TCONCAT: TileType of src and dst tiles must be TileType::Vec.");
    static_assert(TileDst::ValidRow <= TileDst::Rows && TileSrc0::ValidRow <= TileSrc0::Rows &&
                      TileSrc1::ValidRow <= TileSrc1::Rows,
                  "TCONCAT: Number of valid rows must not be greater than number of tile rows.");
    static_assert(std::is_same<idxType, int32_t>::value || std::is_same<idxType, int16_t>::value ||
                      std::is_same<idxType, int8_t>::value || std::is_same<idxType, uint32_t>::value ||
                      std::is_same<idxType, uint16_t>::value || std::is_same<idxType, uint8_t>::value,
                  "TCONCAT: Invalid data type of src0Idx.");

    unsigned validRow = dst.GetValidRow();
    unsigned dstValidCol = dst.GetValidCol();

    PTO_ASSERT(validRow == src0.GetValidRow(), "TCONCAT: validRow of src0 must match dst.");
    PTO_ASSERT(validRow == src1.GetValidRow(), "TCONCAT: validRow of src1 must match dst.");

    TConcatIdx<TileDst, TileSrc0, TileSrc1, TileSrc0Idx, TileSrc1Idx>(
        dst.data(), src0.data(), src1.data(), src0Idx.data(), src1Idx.data(), validRow, dstValidCol);
}
```

Without an official MLIR/PTOAS counterpart, this A5 capability cannot be represented directly in PTO IR or exposed consistently to higher layers.

### Proposed API / behavior

Please add an official PTO op form for indexed tile concat.

Possible IR shape:

```mlir
pto.tconcat ins(%src0, %src1, %src0_idx, %src1_idx :
  !pto.tile_buf<...>, !pto.tile_buf<...>, !pto.tile_buf<...>, !pto.tile_buf<...>)
  outs(%dst : !pto.tile_buf<...>)
```

If overloading `pto.tconcat` is undesirable, a dedicated op name such as `pto.tconcat_idx` would also work. The important part is to expose the indexed A5 semantics in the official dialect.

Suggested verifier expectations based on the C++ contract:
- `dst`, `src0`, and `src1` must have the same data type.
- `src0Idx` and `src1Idx` must have the same index type.
- data types should match the supported C++ set: `i8/i16/i32/u8/u16/u32/f16/bf16/f32`.
- index types should match the supported C++ set: `i8/i16/i32/u8/u16/u32`.
- all participating tiles should be in `loc=vec`.
- `validRow(src0) == validRow(src1) == validRow(dst)`.
- index tile shape / valid-shape constraints should be defined explicitly for MLIR.

### Alternatives considered

Lowering this pattern through a sequence of other ops internally may be possible, but there is still a frontend / dialect gap today: the official PTO surface has no way to express the indexed `TCONCAT_IMPL(dst, src0, src1, src0Idx, src1Idx)` form.

### Additional context

This request is specifically about aligning official PTOAS with the existing A5 C++ PTO ISA surface, so that the indexed concat capability is representable and testable in official PTO IR.

title: [Bug] 对齐 tcolargmax/tcolargmin 的类型约束
body:
### Component

PTO Dialect verifier / `tcolargmax` / `tcolargmin`

### Problem

当前 `pto.tcolargmax` / `pto.tcolargmin` 的 verifier 将 `src` 元素类型限制为 `f16/f32`，但底层 C++ `TColReduceIdxCheck` 的输入约束允许 1/2/4 字节元素类型，因此两者不一致。

这会导致 `ui16/ui32` 等类型在前端 verifier 阶段被拒绝，即使按底层约束它们应当是合法输入。

### Expected behavior

`pto.tcolargmax` / `pto.tcolargmin` 的类型约束应与底层 `TColReduceIdxCheck` 对齐：

- `src/tmp` 允许 1/2/4 字节元素类型
- `dst` 允许 `i32/ui32`
- 其余 layout / valid shape / valid row/col 约束保持现有语义

### Current verifier behavior

当前实现中，以下 verifier 将 `src` 限为 `f16/f32`：

- `lib/PTO/IR/PTO.cpp` 中 `TColArgMaxOp::verify()`
- `lib/PTO/IR/PTO.cpp` 中 `TColArgMinOp::verify()`

关键逻辑如下：

```c++
auto srcElem = getElemTy(srcTy).dyn_cast<mlir::FloatType>();
if (!srcElem || (!srcElem.isF16() && !srcElem.isF32()))
  return emitOpError("expects src element type to be f16 or f32");
```

### Backend-side constraint

底层 C++ `TColReduceIdxCheck` 允许的输入/输出约束为：

```c++
static_assert((sizeof(typename TileDataIn::DType) == 1) ||
              (sizeof(typename TileDataIn::DType) == 2) ||
              (sizeof(typename TileDataIn::DType) == 4),
              "Fix: TCOLREDUCEIDX data type must be b8/b16/b32");
static_assert(std::is_same_v<typename TileDataOut::DType, uint32_t> ||
              std::is_same_v<typename TileDataOut::DType, int32_t>,
              "Fix: TCOLREDUCEIDX output data type must be s32 or u32.");
```

### Minimal reproduction

保存为 `repro.pto`：

```mlir
module {
  func.func @repro_ui16() {
    %src = pto.alloc_tile : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=ui16, rows=16, cols=32, v_row=16, v_col=32, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>
    %tmp = pto.alloc_tile : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=ui16, rows=16, cols=32, v_row=16, v_col=32, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>
    %dst = pto.alloc_tile : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=ui32, rows=1, cols=32, v_row=1, v_col=32, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>

    pto.tcolargmax ins(%src, %tmp : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=ui16, rows=16, cols=32, v_row=16, v_col=32, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>, !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=ui16, rows=16, cols=32, v_row=16, v_col=32, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>)
                   outs(%dst : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=ui32, rows=1, cols=32, v_row=1, v_col=32, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>)
    return
  }
}
```

执行命令：

```bash
ptoas --pto-arch=a5 repro.pto
```

实际结果：

```text
error: 'pto.tcolargmax' op expects src element type to be f16 or f32
```

### Why this looks like a real issue

- 本地最小复现可稳定触发该报错
- `f16` 对照用例可以通过
- EmitC lowering 只是直接发 `TCOLARGMAX/TCOLARGMIN`，类型限制主要来自前端 verifier，而不是 lowering 阶段

### Suggested fix

将 `tcolargmax/tcolargmin` 的 verifier 类型检查从“只允许 `f16/f32`”调整为“允许 1/2/4 字节输入元素类型”，并补充 `ui16/ui32` 等回归测试，保证与底层 `TColReduceIdxCheck` 保持一致。

### Reference

相关问题：
- mouliangyu/PTOAS#211

title: [Issue #546] fix: reject non-lowerable mat tfillpad tile mismatch
body:
## 问题背景
- issue #546 中，pto.tfillpad 在 src/dst 为 loc=mat 且 tile 类型不一致（典型为 v_row/v_col/pad 不一致）时，前端未报错，最终在 C++ 编译阶段报 TFILLPAD 模板匹配失败，定位困难。

## 定位分析
- pto.tfillpad 的 verifier 仅检查了静态 shape 与元素字节宽，未覆盖会影响 Tile<...> 模板特化的一致性字段。
- EmitC 会直接降为 TFILLPAD(dst, src)。对于 loc=mat，仅有同构重载可用，src/dst Tile 类型不一致时无法匹配。
- tfillpad_expand 在 loc=mat 的跨层 ABI（异构 src/dst expand）约束尚未最终定版，本次不改变其行为边界。

## 解决方案
- 在 verifyTFillPadLike 中新增 pto.tfillpad + loc=mat 的 lowerability 检查：当 src/dst TileBufType 不一致时，前端直接报错。
- 诊断中显式列出不一致字段（v_row/v_col/pad）并附带 src/dst 类型与提示（heterogeneous TFILLPAD 仅支持 loc=vec）。
- 同步文档：更新 docs/PTO_IR_manual.md 与 ReleaseNotes.md，明确 loc=mat 下 tfillpad 要求 src/dst 的 validShape 与 pad 完全一致。
- 对 tfillpad_expand 在文档和代码注释中补充当前范围说明，避免误解为已覆盖同类校验。
- 回归验证：cmake --build build --target check-pto -j8（124/124 通过）。

title: [Bug] Consecutive live pto.tpop_from_aiv results are lowered to the same C++ tile object
body:
### Component

EmitC / Codegen (lib/PTO/Transforms/PTOToEmitC.cpp)

### Description

PTOAS v0.28 appears to mis-lower valid `.pto` when two `pto.tpop_from_aiv` results are both still live.

In the `.pto`, the two `tpop` operations produce distinct SSA values and each value is consumed later by a different `pto.tmov`. But in the generated C++, both `TPOP`s write into the same tile object, so the first popped value is overwritten before its consumer runs.

This was observed on an a2a3 cross-core V2C case. The `.pto` itself is correct; the aliasing is introduced only in the generated C++, so this looks like a PTOAS lowering bug rather than an upstream IR bug.

Related: #541. That issue is about nondeterministic allocator/codegen aliasing across repeated runs. This one is deterministic: a single valid `.pto` is lowered into incorrect C++ that aliases two simultaneously-live `tpop` results.

### Reproduction (minimal)

Environment:

- PTOAS release: `v0.28`
- PTOAS commit: `d09562b0a3fdea95f082b6a1eab6f5c03f927df2`
- PyPTO reproducer commit: `c5b462bd8355b4a5dbcd4995f481785e1bf96c42`
- Host: `Linux (aarch64)`
- Target arch: `a3`

Relevant `.pto` fragment (two distinct SSA results remain live at the same time):

```mlir
%received_add__ssa_v0 = pto.tpop_from_aiv {split = 1} -> !pto.tile_buf<loc=mat, dtype=f16, rows=16, cols=16, v_row=16, v_col=16, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>
%received_sub__ssa_v0 = pto.tpop_from_aiv {split = 1} -> !pto.tile_buf<loc=mat, dtype=f16, rows=16, cols=16, v_row=16, v_col=16, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>

pto.tmov ins(%received_add__ssa_v0 : !pto.tile_buf<loc=mat, dtype=f16, rows=16, cols=16, v_row=16, v_col=16, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>) outs(%received_add_left__ssa_v0 : !pto.tile_buf<loc=left, dtype=f16, rows=16, cols=16, v_row=16, v_col=16, blayout=col_major, slayout=row_major, fractal=512, pad=0>)
pto.tmov ins(%received_sub__ssa_v0 : !pto.tile_buf<loc=mat, dtype=f16, rows=16, cols=16, v_row=16, v_col=16, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>) outs(%received_sub_right__ssa_v0 : !pto.tile_buf<loc=right, dtype=f16, rows=16, cols=16, v_row=16, v_col=16, blayout=row_major, slayout=col_major, fractal=512, pad=0>)
```

But the generated C++ lowers both pops into the same object:

```cpp
Tile<TileType::Mat, half, 16, 16, BLayout::RowMajor, 16, 16, SLayout::NoneBox, 512, PadValue::Null, CompactMode::Null> v13;
TPOP<TPipe<0, Direction::DIR_V2C, 512, 8, 8, false>, Tile<TileType::Mat, half, 16, 16, BLayout::RowMajor, 16, 16, SLayout::NoneBox, 512, PadValue::Null, CompactMode::Null>, TileSplitAxis::TILE_UP_DOWN>(v12, v13);
set_flag(PIPE_MTE2, PIPE_MTE1, EVENT_ID0);
TPOP<TPipe<0, Direction::DIR_V2C, 512, 8, 8, false>, Tile<TileType::Mat, half, 16, 16, BLayout::RowMajor, 16, 16, SLayout::NoneBox, 512, PadValue::Null, CompactMode::Null>, TileSplitAxis::TILE_UP_DOWN>(v12, v13);
set_flag(PIPE_MTE2, PIPE_MTE1, EVENT_ID1);

Tile<TileType::Left, half, 16, 16, BLayout::RowMajor, 16, 16, SLayout::RowMajor, 512, PadValue::Null, CompactMode::Null> v14;
wait_flag(PIPE_MTE2, PIPE_MTE1, EVENT_ID0);
TMOV(v14, v13);

Tile<TileType::Right, half, 16, 16, BLayout::RowMajor, 16, 16, SLayout::ColMajor, 512, PadValue::Null, CompactMode::Null> v15;
wait_flag(PIPE_MTE2, PIPE_MTE1, EVENT_ID1);
TMOV(v15, v13);
```

So the second `TPOP(..., v13)` overwrites the first result before `TMOV(v14, v13)` runs.

### Expected behavior

If two `pto.tpop_from_aiv` results are simultaneously live, PTOAS should preserve them as distinct values in generated C++.

That can be done by:

- allocating distinct tile objects for the distinct live results, or
- using another lowering strategy that preserves value separation correctly

### Actual behavior / error logs

PTOAS lowers two distinct live SSA values to the same generated tile object.

This causes incorrect runtime behavior for the interleaved cross-core pop/free case and makes that pattern unsafe to enable upstream, even though the original `.pto` is valid.

### Git commit

d09562b0a3fdea95f082b6a1eab6f5c03f927df2

### Host platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Target Ascend arch (if relevant)

a3

### PTOAS build level (if relevant)

N/A

title: [Issue #556] fix: prevent live tpop results from being CSE-aliased
body:
fix Issue #556
## 问题背景
- `pto.tpop_from_aiv` 的两个同时存活结果在生成 C++ 时可能被错误合并到同一 tile 变量，导致后一个 `TPOP` 覆盖前一个结果。
- 该问题会破坏后续分别消费两个 pop 结果（如连续 `TMOV`）的语义正确性。

## 定位分析
- `tools/ptoas/ptoas.cpp` 在 `PTOViewToMemref` 之后、`EmitPTO` 之前执行了 `CSE`。
- tpop_from_aiv 先被降成 declare_tile + tpop，declare_tile 再被降成 declare_tile_memref + bind_tile
- `pto.declare_tile` / `pto.declare_tile_memref` 之前被标记为 `Pure`，导致这些“应当具备唯一句柄语义”的占位符 op 在 CSE 下可被错误合并。
- 结果是两个逻辑上独立的 live pop 值最终共享同一个 EmitC tile 变量，出现别名覆盖。

## 解决方案
- 将 `DeclareTileOp` 与 `DeclareTileMemRefOp` 从 `Pure` 改为非 `Pure`，避免在 CSE 中被等价折叠。
- 新增回归测试 `test/lit/pto/issue556_tpop_live_values_no_alias.pto`，覆盖两个连续 `tpop_from_aiv` 同时存活并分别 `tmov` 的场景，检查生成 C++ 中使用两个不同 tile 变量。

title: [Bug] A5 trowargmin may over-count tmp scratch like fixed tprelu vec-overflow issue
body:
### Component

PTO Dialect / Memory Planning

### Description

This looks very similar to the already-fixed A5 `tprelu` tmp-overcount issue from [#531](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/PTOAS/issues/531) / [#542](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/PTOAS/pull/542), but for `pto.trowargmin` and likely `pto.trowargmax`.

On current `hw-native-sys/PTOAS` `main` commit `61f876461292e9fee025a3afa1e99766ea7ced06`:

- `TPReluOp::getEffects` is already A5-special-cased to avoid charging an unused `tmp` scratch in local-memory planning.
- `TRowArgMinOp::getEffects` and `TRowArgMaxOp::getEffects` still unconditionally model `tmp` as `write`:
  - `lib/PTO/IR/PTO.cpp` lines around `9719-9737`
- the op definitions still expose `src, tmp, dst` in ODS:
  - `include/PTO/IR/PTOOps.td` lines around `4918-5000`

Downstream A5 TileLang templates for both ops take `tmp` as a formal operand but do not actually consume it in the template body:

- `trowargmin`: https://github.com/lwwangcgz/PTOAS/blob/3ffbced7fe4dc68ef6b19122d1350b46bf311395/lib/TileOps/trowargmin_template.py#L12-L61
- `trowargmax`: https://github.com/lwwangcgz/PTOAS/blob/3ffbced7fe4dc68ef6b19122d1350b46bf311395/lib/TileOps/trowargmax_template.py#L12-L61

That makes this look like the same root cause as `tprelu`: the planner may be charging a full-sized `tmp` scratch tile on A5 even though the A5 implementation path does not need it.

### Reproduction (minimal)

This single-function repro comes from shrinking a downstream ST case into one PTO function:

```mlir
module {
  func.func @TROWARGMIN_TMP_OVERFLOW(%src_ptr: !pto.ptr<f32>, %dst_ptr: !pto.ptr<ui32>) {
    %c0 = arith.constant 0 : index
    %c1 = arith.constant 1 : index
    %c2_r = arith.constant 2 : index
    %c16384_c = arith.constant 16384 : index
    %c32768_se = arith.constant 32768 : index
    %c2_de = arith.constant 2 : index
    %c1_dc = arith.constant 1 : index
    %c2_vr = arith.constant 2 : index
    %c16381_vc = arith.constant 16381 : index
    %src_view = pto.make_tensor_view %src_ptr,
      shape = [%c1, %c1, %c1, %c2_r, %c16384_c],
      strides = [%c32768_se, %c32768_se, %c32768_se, %c16384_c, %c1]
      : !pto.tensor_view<1x1x1x2x16384xf32>
    %dst_view = pto.make_tensor_view %dst_ptr,
      shape = [%c1, %c1, %c1, %c2_r, %c1_dc],
      strides = [%c2_de, %c2_de, %c2_de, %c1_dc, %c1]
      : !pto.tensor_view<1x1x1x2x1xui32>
    %src_part = pto.partition_view %src_view,
      offsets = [%c0, %c0, %c0, %c0, %c0],
      sizes = [%c1, %c1, %c1, %c2_vr, %c16381_vc]
      : !pto.tensor_view<1x1x1x2x16384xf32> -> !pto.partition_tensor_view<1x1x1x2x16381xf32>
    %dst_part = pto.partition_view %dst_view,
      offsets = [%c0, %c0, %c0, %c0, %c0],
      sizes = [%c1, %c1, %c1, %c2_vr, %c1]
      : !pto.tensor_view<1x1x1x2x1xui32> -> !pto.partition_tensor_view<1x1x1x2x1xui32>
    %src = pto.alloc_tile
      : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f32, rows=2, cols=16384, v_row=2, v_col=16381,
                      blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>
    %tmp = pto.alloc_tile
      : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f32, rows=2, cols=16384, v_row=2, v_col=16381,
                      blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>
    %dst = pto.alloc_tile
      : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=ui32, rows=2, cols=1, v_row=2, v_col=1,
                      blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>
    pto.tload ins(%src_part : !pto.partition_tensor_view<1x1x1x2x16381xf32>)
              outs(%src : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f32, rows=2, cols=16384, v_row=2, v_col=16381,
                                      blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>)
    pto.trowargmin ins(%src, %tmp : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f32, rows=2, cols=16384, v_row=2, v_col=16381,
                                            blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>,
                                !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f32, rows=2, cols=16384, v_row=2, v_col=16381,
                                            blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>)
                    outs(%dst : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=ui32, rows=2, cols=1, v_row=2, v_col=1,
                                             blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>)
    pto.tstore ins(%dst : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=ui32, rows=2, cols=1, v_row=2, v_col=1,
                                     blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>)
               outs(%dst_part : !pto.partition_tensor_view<1x1x1x2x1xui32>)
    return
  }
}
```

Run:

```bash
./build/tools/ptoas/ptoas \
  --pto-arch=a5 \
  --pto-backend=vpto \
  --enable-insert-sync \
  --enable-tile-op-expand \
  --vpto-emit-hivm-llvm \
  issue_trowargmin_tmp_vec_overflow_repro.pto \
  -o -
```

### Expected behavior

If A5 `trowargmin` really does not need a full-sized `tmp` scratch, this should compile successfully after local-memory planning models only the buffers actually required on A5, similar to the `tprelu` fix in #542.

### Actual behavior / error logs

On downstream reproduction this fails with:

```text
loc("issue_trowargmin_tmp_vec_overflow_repro.pto":2:3): error: vec overflow, requires 2097408 bits while 2031616 bits avaliable!
Error: Pass execution failed.
```

### Notes

- The reported `2097408 bits` is almost exactly `2 * (2 * 16384 * 32)` plus a very small remainder:
  - one `f32[2 x 16384]` tile is `1048576 bits`
  - two such tiles are `2097152 bits`
  - reported total is `2097408 bits`
- That makes the failure look consistent with the planner charging both `src` and a full-sized `tmp`, even though the A5 lowering/template body does not appear to consume `tmp`.
- `TRowArgMaxOp` looks structurally identical in `getEffects`, so it may need the same audit/fix even if this issue is fixed first via `trowargmin`.

title: fix(pto): avoid false A5 trowarg vec overflow
body:
## Summary
- avoid charging `tmp` as a scratch write for A5 `pto.trowargmin`
- avoid charging `tmp` as a scratch write for A5 `pto.trowargmax`
- add A5 regression tests for the false vec-overflow repros

## Root Cause
A5 row-arg reduction lowering does not consume the full-size `tmp` scratch tile, but memory effects still modeled `tmp` as a write operand. That inflated local-memory planning and could trigger false `vec overflow` diagnostics, matching the pattern previously fixed for `tprelu` in #542.

title: [Issue #554] fix: align tcolarg verifier with backend input width constraints
body:
## 问题背景
- pto.tcolargmax / pto.tcolargmin 的 verifier 之前将 src 限制为 f16/f32，与底层 TColReduceIdxCheck 的 1/2/4 字节输入约束不一致。
- 导致 ui16/ui32 等按后端约束本应合法的输入在前端 verifier 阶段被错误拒绝。

## 定位分析
- 类型限制集中在 verifyTColArgReductionOpCommon，原逻辑要求 src 必须是 FloatType 且仅允许 f16/f32。
- tmp 与 src 的同类型约束、dst 为 i32/ui32、以及 layout/valid-shape 相关约束本身合理，无需调整。

## 解决方案
- 将 tcolargmax/tcolargmin 的 src 类型检查放宽为：任意整数或浮点类型，且元素位宽仅允许 8/16/32（即 1/2/4 字节）。
- 保持 dst 必须是 i32/ui32 的约束不变。
- 新增回归测试 test/lit/pto/issue554_tcolarg_ui16_emitc.pto，覆盖：
- tcolargmax 使用 ui16 -> ui32
- tcolargmin 使用 ui16 -> i32
- 本地验证：llvm-lit --filter issue554_tcolarg_ui16_emitc|tcolargmax_emitc|tcolargmin_emitc 通过（3/3）。

title: [InsertSync] fix zero-trip loop unsoundness without dropping cross-re…
body:
…gion syncs

Refines the zero-trip fix from PR #540 (issue #533) so it stops breaking cross-region producer/consumer pairing around loops and no-else branches (issue #564).

Background
----------
PR #540 addressed issue #533 (missing MTE2->V barrier after a loop that may execute zero iterations) by disabling *all* propagation of SyncRecord state from a loop body back to the enclosing scope. The stated concern was that `syncFinder` participates in `alreadySync` inference later (`UpdateSyncRecord`), so propagating it would still be unsound on the zero-trip path.

That cut is too broad. `syncFinder` visibility at the outer scope is also used by `InsertSeqSync` to pair post-loop consumers with producers living inside the body (e.g. the four `wait_flag(PIPE_MTE1, PIPE_MTE2, ...)` drains after the Qwen3 K-loop pipelined GEMM, and the matching pre-loop seeds). With all propagation suppressed, those cross-region syncs vanish too, which is exactly the 0.27 -> 0.29 regression reported in issue #564. The PR's own test update for `issue454_nested_loop_same_pipe_pair_regression` -- which silently dropped the pre-loop `set_flag` CHECKs -- was an early symptom of this over-reach.

Fix
---
Narrow the cut to the exact step that is unsound on zero-trip paths.

1. Add `SyncRecord::syncFinderIsConditional`, a parallel DenseMap that tags a `syncFinder[idx]` entry as "populated inside a region that may not execute" (loop body or no-else branch).

2. In `UpdateSyncRecord`, guard the transitive-elevation step so a SET cannot elevate `alreadySync` via a conditional finder. On the zero-trip / zero-branch path this preserves the issue #533 invariant.

3. In `InsertLoopSync`, restore `syncFinder` propagation from the body back to the outer state, but mark body-introduced entries as conditional. Continue to NOT propagate `alreadySync`.

4. In `InsertBranchSync` no-else path, apply the same conditional tagging to `syncFinder` entries introduced by the then-branch, extending the zero-trip protection to zero-branch paths.

Testing
-------
Local diff review only. Covered by existing lit tests:

* issue533_loop_zero_trip_sync_regression.pto (PR #540) -- still expected to pass: body-interior WAIT is now tagged conditional on propagation, so the outer SET no longer elevates MTE2 alreadySync and the post-loop MTE2->V barrier is preserved.
* issue454_nested_loop_same_pipe_pair_regression.pto -- pre-loop set_flag(PIPE_M, PIPE_MTE1, EVENT_ID[OUT/IN]) CHECKs restored, since they describe the correct loop-carried seed behavior that PR #540 suppressed.

Follow-up: add a minimized K-loop L1-Mat recycle regression test derived from the Qwen3 scope3_incore_0 reproducer in issue #564.

Build verification by reviewers is recommended before merge; the submitter was unable to run the InsertSync lit suite end-to-end.

Refs: #533, #564

title: [Bug] `pto.subview` rejects column subviews of MAT/RIGHT tiles
body:
### Component

Verifier / IR semantics (lib/PTO/IR)

### Description

The `pto.subview` verifier rejects any column subview of a boxed RowMajor
`pto.tile_buf` whose memory space is `MAT` or `RIGHT`, with:

```
'pto.subview' op boxed RowMajor subview must keep full cols
```

The same shape pattern works for `ACC` tiles. This blocks the natural
expression of the pto-isa flash-attention `kTileFactor=N` pattern, where one
wide K tile on the cube side is reused by N narrower QK matmuls writing into
column subviews of a wide ACC tile. The only workaround we found is to
allocate N independent narrow MAT/RIGHT tiles and issue N separate GM
`slice_view` loads, which adds MTE2 traffic and forfeits MAT-side ping-pong
on K — defeating the optimization.



### Reproduction (minimal)

| case        | what it does                                       | result                          |
|-------------|----------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------|
| `ok_acc`    | column subviews of a wide **ACC** tile             | ✅ ptoas + bisheng lower cleanly |
| `bad_mat`   | column subviews of a wide boxed RowMajor **MAT**   | ❌ verifier error                |
| `bad_right` | column subviews of a wide **RIGHT** tile           | ❌ verifier error                |

The python script below asserts:

- `ok_acc` produces a module that verifies and contains `pto.subview`;
- `bad_mat` and `bad_right` raise `MLIRError` carrying
  "`boxed RowMajor subview must keep full cols`" and the offending memory
  space in the verifier note.

Run it with:

```bash
pytest tests/frontend/test_subview_verifier.py -v
```

```python
"""Low-level MLIR-binding reproducer / unit test for the verifier rule

    'pto.subview' op boxed RowMajor subview must keep full cols

This file calls `mlir.dialects.pto` and `mlir.ir` directly so the failure surface is just the
ptoas dialect's own type/op constructors and the MLIR module verifier.

* ``ok_acc``   — column subview of a wide ACC tile      → must verify
* ``bad_mat``  — column subview of a wide MAT tile      → must FAIL verifier
* ``bad_right``— column subview of a wide RIGHT tile    → must FAIL verifier

"""
import pytest

from mlir.ir import (
    Context,
    F16Type,
    F32Type,
    InsertionPoint,
    Location,
    MLIRError,
    Module,
)
from mlir.dialects import func, pto as _pto


# --- Tile-type builders ------------------------------------------------------

def _cfg(blayout, slayout, s_fractal_size, pad="Null"):
    return _pto.TileBufConfigAttr.get(
        _pto.BLayoutAttr.get(getattr(_pto.BLayout, blayout)),
        _pto.SLayoutAttr.get(getattr(_pto.SLayout, slayout)),
        s_fractal_size,
        _pto.PadValueAttr.get(getattr(_pto.PadValue, pad)),
    )


def _tile_buf_type(*, shape, dtype, space, config):
    space_attr = _pto.AddressSpaceAttr.get(getattr(_pto.AddressSpace, space))
    return _pto.TileBufType.get(shape, dtype, space_attr, shape, config)


# --- Per-case kernel builders -----------------------------------------------

def _build(case: str) -> Module:
    """Build a single-cube-kernel module for `case` and return it.

    Raises ``MLIRError`` from ``module.operation.verify()`` for the bad cases.
    """
    with Context() as ctx, Location.unknown():
        _pto.register_dialect(ctx, load=True)
        fp16 = F16Type.get()
        fp32 = F32Type.get()

        S0, HEAD, W, WIDE = 32, 32, 256, 512

        ab_size = _pto.TileConfig.fractalABSize
        c_size = _pto.TileConfig.fractalCSize

        # "Boxed RowMajor" K-transpose configs (blayout=RowMajor) — these are
        # the ones the verifier guards. They mirror the k_mat_ty / k_right_ty
        # used by the flash_attention cube kernel.
        mat_cfg = _cfg("RowMajor", "ColMajor", ab_size)
        right_cfg = _cfg("RowMajor", "ColMajor", ab_size)
        left_cfg = _cfg("RowMajor", "RowMajor", ab_size)
        acc_cfg = _cfg("ColMajor", "RowMajor", c_size)

        m = Module.create()
        with InsertionPoint(m.body):
            fty = func.FunctionType.get([], [])
            f = func.FuncOp("cube_kernel", fty)
            f.operation.attributes["pto.kernel_kind"] = (
                __import__("mlir.ir", fromlist=["Attribute"]).Attribute.parse(
                    "#pto.kernel_kind<cube>"
                )
            )
            blk = f.add_entry_block()
            with InsertionPoint(blk):
                if case == "ok_acc":
                    qk_acc_wide_ty = _tile_buf_type(
                        shape=[S0, WIDE], dtype=fp32, space="ACC", config=acc_cfg
                    )
                    qk = _pto.AllocTileOp(qk_acc_wide_ty).result
                    c0 = _const_index(0)
                    cW = _const_index(W)
                    # Two column subviews of the ACC tile -- must verify.
                    _pto.subview(qk, [c0, c0], [S0, W])
                    _pto.subview(qk, [c0, cW], [S0, W])

                elif case == "bad_mat":
                    k_mat_wide_ty = _tile_buf_type(
                        shape=[HEAD, WIDE], dtype=fp16, space="MAT", config=mat_cfg
                    )
                    k_mat = _pto.AllocTileOp(k_mat_wide_ty).result
                    c0 = _const_index(0)
                    cW = _const_index(W)
                    # The two offending subviews:
                    _pto.subview(k_mat, [c0, c0], [HEAD, W])
                    _pto.subview(k_mat, [c0, cW], [HEAD, W])

                elif case == "bad_right":
                    k_right_wide_ty = _tile_buf_type(
                        shape=[HEAD, WIDE], dtype=fp16, space="RIGHT", config=right_cfg
                    )
                    k_right = _pto.AllocTileOp(k_right_wide_ty).result
                    c0 = _const_index(0)
                    cW = _const_index(W)
                    # The two offending subviews:
                    _pto.subview(k_right, [c0, c0], [HEAD, W])
                    _pto.subview(k_right, [c0, cW], [HEAD, W])

                else:  # pragma: no cover - guard
                    raise ValueError(f"unknown case {case!r}")

                func.ReturnOp([])

        m.operation.verify()
        return m


def _const_index(value: int):
    from mlir.dialects import arith
    from mlir.ir import IndexType, IntegerAttr

    return arith.ConstantOp(IndexType.get(), IntegerAttr.get(IndexType.get(), value)).result


# --- Tests -------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_acc_column_subview_verifies():
    """ACC column subviews are valid IR: must verify and contain pto.subview."""
    m = _build("ok_acc")
    asm = str(m)
    assert "pto.subview" in asm, asm
    # Sanity: the ACC tile is 32x512 and we carve two 32x256 subviews.
    assert "32x512xf32" in asm, asm
    assert asm.count("32x256xf32") >= 2, asm


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "case,space_str",
    [
        ("bad_mat", "mat"),
        ("bad_right", "right"),
    ],
)
def test_boxed_rowmajor_column_subview_rejected(case, space_str):

    with pytest.raises(MLIRError) as exc_info:
        _build(case)

    msg = str(exc_info.value)
    assert "pto.subview" in msg, msg
    assert "boxed RowMajor subview must keep full cols" in msg, msg
    # The op type printed in the verifier note must mention the right space.
    assert space_str in msg, msg

```

### Expected behavior

`bad_mat` and `bad_right` should lower analogously to `ok_acc`: column
subviews of a wide MAT/RIGHT `tile_buf` should be valid IR, allowing one
wide K-load to feed N narrower matmuls (or N narrower `mov`s into RIGHT)
without re-issuing the GM load.

Equivalently: please relax the "boxed RowMajor subview must keep full cols"
rule for MAT and RIGHT, or document why it is fundamental and what the
recommended pattern is for sharing one wide K-load across N narrow matmuls
on the cube side.


### Actual behavior / error logs

`bad_mat`:

```bash
mlir._mlir_libs._site_initialize.<locals>.MLIRError: Verification failed:
error: unknown: 'pto.subview' op boxed RowMajor subview must keep full cols
 note: unknown: see current operation:
   %5 = "pto.subview"(%2, %0, %0)
        <{operandSegmentSizes = array<i32: 1, 2, 0, 0>, sizes = [32, 256]}>
        : (!pto.tile_buf<mat, 32x512xf16, slayout=col_major>, index, index)
        -> !pto.tile_buf<mat, 32x256xf16, slayout=col_major>
```

`bad_right`:

```bash
mlir._mlir_libs._site_initialize.<locals>.MLIRError: Verification failed:
error: unknown: 'pto.subview' op boxed RowMajor subview must keep full cols
 note: unknown: see current operation:
   %6 = "pto.subview"(%3, %0, %0)
        <{operandSegmentSizes = array<i32: 1, 2, 0, 0>, sizes = [32, 256]}>
        : (!pto.tile_buf<right, 32x512xf16, slayout=col_major>, index, index)
        -> !pto.tile_buf<right, 32x256xf16, slayout=col_major>
```

`ok_acc` lowers and builds end-to-end with `ptoas --pto-arch=a3
--enable-insert-sync`.


### Git commit

a03d8fdcc23e40e9db6d2e8f21869f10cde7ef71

Linux (aarch64)

a3

[Feature] Expose `CV_FIFO_CONS_SYNC_PERIOD` (batched FFTS sync) on `pto.{aic,aiv}_initialize_pipe` and `pto.initialize_l2g2l_pipe`
body:
### Summary

The pto-isa flash-attention reference kernel skips FFTS sync on
`(N-1)` of every `N` push/pop iterations via a compile-time period
parameter (`FiFoSyncT` on `TMPipe`, surfaced as
`kFaCvFifoConsSyncPeriod = kFaCvFifoSize / 2 = 4`). The producer- and
consumer-side state machines toggle their `setAllocateStatus` /
`setRecordStatus` / `setWaitStatus` / `setFreeStatus` flags based on
this period so the underlying FFTS event is only allocated/waited/
recorded/freed once per `N` slots.

The three ptoas pipe-initialization ops have **no attribute** to express
this. As a result every pipe instantiated through ptoas runs at
period=1 (one FFTS event per slot), which we cannot match to the
hand-tuned reference and which dominates sync overhead on hot
QK / PV pipes.

We would like ptoas to add a `cons_sync_period` (name negotiable) integer
attribute on:

- `pto.AicInitializePipeOp`
- `pto.AivInitializePipeOp`
- `pto.InitializeL2G2LPipeOp`

defaulting to `1` (current behavior), and forward it to the same
`FiFoSyncT` knob the reference uses.

### Motivation / use case

Concrete consumer: the flash-attention kernel under
[`examples/aot/flash_attention/`](https://github.com/huawei-csl/pto-dsl/blob/main/examples/aot/flash_attention/) — see §2 of its [README](https://github.com/huawei-csl/pto-dsl/blob/main/examples/aot/flash_attention/README.md). At `(Q_ROWS=2048, S1=8192, HEAD=32)` we currently sit at **0.94×** of
`npu_fused_infer_attention_score`. The reference kernel hits its
performance largely because its hot QK / PV pipes pay one FFTS sync
event per 4 slots, not per slot.

Reference kernel locations in
[`pto-isa/kernels/manual/common/flash_atten/`](https://gitcode.com/cann/pto-isa/blob/master/kernels/manual/common/flash_atten/fa_performance_kernel.cpp):

- **Period definition** — `fa_performance_kernel.h:19-20`
  ```cpp
  constexpr int kFaCvFifoSize = 8;
  constexpr int kFaCvFifoConsSyncPeriod = kFaCvFifoSize / 2;   // = 4
  ```
- **Pipe-type instantiation** — `fa_performance_kernel.cpp:780-783`
  ```cpp
  constexpr uint8_t FiFoDepth = CV_FIFO_SIZE;
  constexpr uint8_t FiFoSyncT = CV_FIFO_CONS_SYNC_PERIOD;
  using QKPipe = TMPipe<BUF0_QK_READY, FIFOType::GM_FIFO,
                        FiFoDepth, FiFoSyncT, ...>;
  ```
- **Effect on the producer/consumer state machine**
  - `:298, :436, :524` —
    `should_wait_consumption<DEPTH, PERIOD>(sync_iter)` →
    `pvPipe.prod.setAllocateStatus(...)` (`:437`),
    `setRecordStatus(true)` (`:438`).
  - `:376, :476, :567` —
    `should_notify_consumption<DEPTH, PERIOD>(sync_iter)` →
    `pvPipe.cons.setFreeStatus(...)` (`:569`),
    `setWaitStatus(true)` (`:568`).
- **Drain accounting** — `:885, :888`
  `pending_consumption_events(num_tiles_s1, fifo_size, PERIOD)`.

Without an equivalent parameter in ptoas, every kernel built on top of it
inherits the period=1 overhead.

**Expected impact:** ~15–25% reduction of FFTS sync overhead on
flash-attention-style kernels that hot-loop on pipe push/pop (per the
reference kernel design notes).




### Proposed API / behavior

Add an optional integer attribute (default `1`) to the three pipe-init
ops, e.g. `cons_sync_period`, and lower it to the same `FiFoSyncT`
template knob the reference kernel uses (or whatever runtime equivalent
the auto-generated pipe machinery has):

```mlir
%pipe = pto.initialize_l2g2l_pipe
    {dir_mask = 1,
     slot_size = 1024,
     slot_num = 8,
     cons_sync_period = 4}    // <-- new, default = 1
    (%gm_addr, %local_addr)
    : (...) -> !pto.pipe
```

Semantics: when `cons_sync_period = N`, only `iter % N == N-1` push/pop
sites perform `setAllocate`/`setRecord` (producer) and
`setWait`/`setFree` (consumer); the other `(N-1)` iterations skip them,
matching the `should_{wait,notify}_consumption<DEPTH, N>` helpers in the
reference.

Constraints we'd expect ptoas to validate (mirroring the reference):

- `cons_sync_period >= 1`.
- `slot_num % cons_sync_period == 0` (so the pipeline drains cleanly).
- A static-assert / verifier diag if the attribute is set on a pipe
  configuration where the underlying machinery cannot honor it.


### Alternatives considered

1. **User-side coalescing of `tpush` / `tpop` calls.** Doesn't work:
   the FFTS event is allocated by the pipe-init op itself; pushes/pops
   only choose which slot to address. The DSL has no way to tell the
   FFTS layer "skip the wait this iteration".
2. **Manual `wait_flag` / `set_flag` from the DSL.** Would require
   bypassing the pipe abstraction entirely and re-implementing the
   reference's producer/consumer state machine in user code, defeating
   the purpose of the high-level pipe op.
3. **Bumping `slot_num`.** Independent axis: more slots gives a deeper
   pipeline but still costs one FFTS event per slot. The reference uses
   `slot_num = 8` *and* `period = 4`; the two compose.

### Additional context

Today's APIs:

```
AicInitializePipeOp
  (self, dir_mask, slot_size, c2v_consumer_buf, v2c_consumer_buf, *,
   id=None, nosplit=None, gm_slot_buffer=None, loc=None, ip=None)

AivInitializePipeOp
  (self, dir_mask, slot_size, c2v_consumer_buf, v2c_consumer_buf, *,
   id=None, nosplit=None, gm_slot_buffer=None, loc=None, ip=None)

InitializeL2G2LPipeOp
  (self, dir_mask, slot_size, slot_num, gm_addr, local_addr, *,
   local_slot_num=None, flag_base=None, nosplit=None,
   peer_local_addr=None, loc=None, ip=None)

MISSING consumer-ack-period kwarg on:
  AicInitializePipeOp, AivInitializePipeOp, InitializeL2G2LPipeOp
```

### Environment

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| pto-dsl commit | `a03d8fdcc23e40e9db6d2e8f21869f10cde7ef71` |
| Host | `Linux  aarch64` |
| Target Ascend arch | `a3` (`bisheng --npu-arch=dav-2201`) |
| ptoas | `0.29` |
| bisheng | `clang 15.0.5 (clang-5c68a1cb1231 flang-5c68a1cb1231)` |

title: feat(pto): add indexed tconcat op (tconcatidx)
body:
## Summary

Add `pto.tconcatidx` to the PTO dialect, supporting the indexed concat form that takes two additional index tile operands (`src0Idx`, `src1Idx`) to control per-row column counts during concatenation.

Closes #550.

## Changes

| Layer | File | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| ODS | `include/PTO/IR/PTOOps.td` | `TConcatidxOp` with 5 operands (src0, src1, src0Idx, src1Idx, dst) |
| Verifier | `lib/PTO/IR/PTO.cpp` | type consistency, loc=vec, row-major, valid_row alignment, index cols >= 1, element type checks |
| EmitC lowering | `lib/PTO/Transforms/PTOToEmitC.cpp` | generates `TCONCAT(dst, src0, src1, src0Idx, src1Idx)` |
| ViewToMemref | `lib/PTO/Transforms/PTOViewToMemref.cpp` | memref type refresh |
| Docs | `docs/PTO_IR_manual.md` | standalone `pto.tconcatidx` section |
| Test | `test/basic/tconcatidx.pto` | lit regression for both plain and indexed forms |

## IR shape

```mlir
pto.tconcatidx ins(%src0, %src1, %idx0, %idx1 :
  !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f32, ...>,
  !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f32, ...>,
  !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=i32, ...>,
  !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=i32, ...>)
  outs(%dst : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f32, ...>)
```

## Verified constraints

- Data types: `i8/i16/i32/f16/f32/bf16` (signless)
- Index types: `i8/i16/i32` (signless)
- All tiles `loc=vec`, row-major, rank-2
- `validRow` matches across all tiles
- Index tile `valid_col >= 1`
- Semantics: `min(idxN_num, srcN_valid_col, dst_valid_col)` to guard source bounds

## Test plan

- [x] Build passes
- [x] `ptoas test/basic/tconcatidx.pto` parses and verifies both forms
- [x] EmitC generates `TCONCAT(dst, src0, src1, src0Idx, src1Idx)`
- [x] Existing concat sample continues to work

title: [Feature] `pto.tpush` / `pto.tpop` — `entry_offset` parameter for sub-slot partial push/pop
body:
### Summary

Add an optional `entry_offset: int = 0` (byte offset) parameter to `pto.tpush`, `pto.tpop`, and their legacy `tpush_to_aiv` / `tpop_from_aic` variants, plus corresponding `allocate` and `record` boolean controls. This exposes the hardware's `setEntryOffset` / `setAllocateStatus` / `setRecordStatus` capabilities already used in [`fa_performance_kernel.cpp`](https://gitcode.com/cann/pto-isa/blob/master/kernels/manual/common/flash_atten/fa_performance_kernel.cpp), allowing a single FIFO slot to be filled and consumed in multiple narrow sub-tile writes rather than one full-width write.

### Motivation / use case

`fa_performance_kernel.cpp` splits each logical K tile (`[HEAD, Tile_S1]`) into `kTileFactor = Tile_S1 / Cube_S1` narrow sub-matmuls. Each sub-matmul operates on a `[HEAD, Cube_S1]` K tile and writes a `[Cube_S0, Cube_S1]` QK result into a different column-offset of the same `[Cube_S0, Tile_S1]` FIFO slot:

```cpp
// kTileFactor = 2, Cube_S1 = 128, Tile_S1 = 256
for (int sub_tile = 0; sub_tile < kTileFactor; sub_tile++) {
    GlobalDataK kGlobal(k + s1_index * HEAD_SIZE);   // narrow [HEAD, Cube_S1] load
    TLOAD(kMatTile[pingpong], kGlobal);
    pto_macro_matmul<Cube_S0, HEAD, Cube_S1>(..., AccMode::InitFinalSum);

    qkPipe.prod.setAllocateStatus(sub_tile == 0 && need_backpressure);
    qkPipe.prod.setRecordStatus(sub_tile == kTileFactor - 1);
    qkPipe.prod.setEntryOffset(sub_tile * Cube_S0 * Cube_S1 * sizeof(float));
    TPUSH(qkAccTile, qkPipe);
}
```

This pattern enables three compounding performance benefits that are impossible to express in the current DSL:

1. **Smaller tile working set** — `[HEAD, Cube_S1]` L0B tiles fit a larger `Cube_K` in `pto_macro_matmul`, reducing TEXTRACT/TMATMUL segment count. At `HEAD=128, Cube_S1=128`: `Cube_K=128`, `kSegments=1` vs `Cube_K=32`, `kSegments=4` for a wide `[HEAD, 512]` tile.
2. **K tile double-buffering** — narrow K tiles (`kMatTNBuffers=2`) let MTE2 load of sub-tile `i+1` overlap with the M matmul of sub-tile `i`. Not possible with a single wide tile.
3. **Smaller ACC footprint** — the ACC tile is `[Cube_S0, Cube_S1]` instead of `[Cube_S0, Tile_S1]`, enabling ACC ping-pong between two L0C addresses.

Without this primitive, the DSL is equivalent to `kTileFactor=1` (one full-width matmul per tile), which is measurably slower at the reference shape `(HEAD=128, Cube_S1=128, Tile_S1=256, QK_PRELOAD=4)`.


### Proposed API / behavior

MLIR op level — add attributes to `pto.tpush` and `pto.tpop`:

```mlir
pto.tpush %qk_acc, %pipe { split = 1 : i8, entry_offset = 0 : i64,
                             allocate = true, record = false }
pto.tpush %qk_acc, %pipe { split = 1 : i8, entry_offset = 32768 : i64,
                             allocate = false, record = true }
```

All three new parameters default to their current implicit values (`entry_offset=0`, `allocate=true`, `record=true`) so all existing call sites are unaffected.

### Alternatives considered

**Column subviews on RIGHT/MAT tile buffers** — load a wide `[HEAD, Tile_S1]` tile and subview it as two `[HEAD, Cube_S1]` rhs operands for two matmuls. ptoas 0.32 removed the MLIR verifier restriction on these subviews, but the `tmatmul` lowering still emits incorrect DMA descriptors for strided RIGHT operands at runtime (separate bug report filed). Even if the codegen were fixed, this approach still loads the full wide tile (same DMA cost), cannot double-buffer K, and measured at **0.94×** vs **0.97×** for the current wide single-matmul path — net negative at our shapes.

### Additional context

- Reference file: `fa_performance_kernel.cpp`, template `runTFA<>`, function `compute_qk`.
- The hardware `TMPipe` already supports all three controls via `setAllocateStatus` / `setRecordStatus` / `setEntryOffset` before each `TPUSH`/`TPOP`. This is a MLIR API surface gap only — no new compiler pass or hardware feature is needed.
- The same `entry_offset` pattern applies to all three FIFO directions in the FA pipeline: QK cube→vec push (column offset by `sub_tile_id`), P vec→cube push (column offset by `row_offset`), and PV cube→vec push (always `entry_offset=0`, included for API consistency).
- This is the primary blocking item for porting `fa_performance_kernel.cpp` to the DSL at its native shape `(HEAD=128, Cube_S1=128, Tile_S1=256, QK_PRELOAD=4)`, which cannot be expressed at all today.

title: [Sync] make may-zero control flow state merge sound
body:
## Summary
- Make insert-sync state path-sensitive by splitting `SyncRecord` into `must` and `may`.
- Use only `must.alreadySync` for elimination decisions, preventing may-path facts from swallowing required waits.
- Fix branch merge semantics:
  - if-else: `must = intersection`, `may = union`
  - if without else: merge then-path with bypass baseline (instead of inheriting then-path-only state).
- Fix loop merge semantics:
  - default: treat loops as may-zero and merge body-exit with baseline (`must` intersect / `may` union)
  - keep legacy aggressive mode behind `--insert-sync-assume-alive-loops`.
- Apply the same must/may semantics to `syncFinder` because it contributes to transitive already-sync inference.

title: [Sync] derive loop event id count from buffer slots
body:
Summary
- Derive loop-carried sync event-id count from actual buffer address slots instead of MAT/VEC address space.
- Preserve all pointer_cast address operands in BaseMemInfo and apply alias offsets to every slot.
- Emit dynamic set/wait flag ops for real ping-pong sync selection.
- Add regression coverage for single-slot vs two-slot loop-carried sync behavior and update affected sync expectations.

Motivation
- The old GetEventIdNum() rule returned 2 for any dependency touching MAT/VEC, which over-consumed event ids and could force unnecessary event-id pressure/fallbacks.

Design
- Single physical address slot => eventIdNum=1.
- Multiple pointer_cast address slots => eventIdNum=2, matching the current ping-pong codegen support.
- Multi-buffer codegen now uses set_flag_dyn/wait_flag_dyn with the selected event id instead of discarding the computed selection.

Testing
- Local: ninja -C build ptoas
- Local: ninja -C build check-pto (137/137 passed)

Risk / Rollback
- Risk: loop-carried sync output changes where tests previously assumed coarse two-id allocation.
- Rollback: revert this PR.

title: Allow different tiles reusing/overlapping same physical address range to save buffer usage
body:
### Summary

[current `fa_performance_kernel.cpp`](https://gitcode.com/cann/pto-isa/blob/fb4dfc4bf0df83e7a4d6a7f959e3fa76018134d1/kernels/manual/common/flash_atten/fa_performance_kernel.cpp#L233) uses `offset = assign_tile_buffers_union(srcTiles, pvTile, offset);` to save UB space when using large tiles. Without this trick, the UB overflows when `S1_TILE>=256`. `S1_TILE<=128` compiles fine, but the performance is not optimal for long sequence.

In ptoas / python binding, UB reuse can be achieved by  `--pto-level=level3` https://github.com/huawei-csl/pto-dsl/pull/126. But then all the tiles need explicit base pointers, making the Python code quite verbose like C++.

### Motivation / use case

To support large-tile flash attention example.

### Reproduce
