title: fix(emitc): rely on pto-inst for communication headers
body:
## Summary

- stop emitting a generated `PIPE_FIX` macro for communication kernels
- remove the redundant direct `pto/comm/pto_comm_inst.hpp` include and rely on the phase-aware `pto/pto-inst.hpp` entry point used by PTO-ISA testcases
- retain the A3 regression that combines a communication op with a real `PIPE_M -> PIPE_FIX` dependency

## Root cause

BiSheng compiles CCE sources in separate host and device phases. PTO-ISA already accounts for this: `pto-inst.hpp` includes `pto_instr.hpp` only for `__CPU_SIM`, `__CCE_AICORE__`, or `__COSTMODEL`, and the device path then obtains communication instructions and the native CANN `PIPE_FIX` enumerator.

PTOAS bypassed that boundary by unconditionally emitting `pto/comm/pto_comm_inst.hpp`. The host phase therefore parsed `event.hpp` even though the host CANN pipe enum does not expose `PIPE_FIX`. The old compatibility macro also aliased `PIPE_FIX` to `PIPE_M`, collapsing real `PIPE_M -> PIPE_FIX` synchronization into `PIPE_M -> PIPE_M`.

## Validation

- focused lit coverage: 7 passed (`issue1086`, comm EmitC, A3 FIX-pipe selection, and related fence regressions)
- full lit suite: 1540 passed / 1 unsupported
- generated Issue #1086 C++ contains only `#include "pto/pto-inst.hpp"`; no generated `PIPE_FIX` macro or direct communication include remains
- the generated `set_flag` / `wait_flag(PIPE_M, PIPE_FIX, ...)` calls are preserved
- the complete generated C++ compiles with the A3 board BiSheng 15.0.5 / CANN 9.0.0 toolchain without any `PIPE_FIX` fallback

Closes #1086

title: Drop a carried dependence proven absent by disjointness
body:
This proves that case for a `pto.partition_view` whose offset is affine in the
enclosing loop's induction variable, and drops the dependence. The proof is in
address space rather than index space: disjoint index ranges imply disjoint
addresses only if the layout maps distinct index tuples to distinct addresses,
which a strided view does not promise. One iteration touches addresses within a
bounded window of its base, and the next iteration's base sits further away than
that window is wide.

The predicate refuses unless every input is a compile-time constant, and refuses
multi-buffered accesses outright: a rotating slot set has a real carried
dependence at the rotation distance, which is a different claim from no dependence
at any distance.

Measured on the sample corpus, 15 sites across 15 files. A further 15 same-pipe
barriers on 7 other kernels are refused, so the predicate discriminates rather
than firing everywhere. Effect on the rope-pack kernel, three runs each:

  A3   35.402 -> 8.980 us   (-74.6%)
  A5   68.990 -> 22.010 us  (-68.1%)

Emitted output is byte-identical on both architectures under randomised inputs
with a poisoned destination buffer.

Four refusal cases are pinned alongside the drop, because a predicate that fired
unconditionally would pass a test that only checked the drop: movement narrower
than the footprint, zero movement, movement the analysis cannot bound, and the
boundary case where movement exactly equals the footprint (adjacent, so disjoint).

title: Added  three absolute synchronization gates ( Correctness tests)
body:
Three checks over the synchronization a compilation emits, each judging one run on its own rather than against a reference:

  G3       every static event and buffer id is one the target permits for that op, direction and arch, and set/wait stay balanced per direction. Rotating ids on set_flag_dyn / wait_flag_dyn resolve at runtime and are not checked.
  
  G2       for a given id key the live intervals are pairwise disjoint. Event ids are keyed by (srcPipe, dstPipe, id) because event flags are
per-direction disjoint hardware, so EVENT_ID0 may be live in MTE2->V and V->MTE3 at once; keying on the id alone would raise a false
     violation on correct code.
     
  G1-self  every dependence the front-end analysis reports is ordered by emitted sync, derived from DepBetween directly. Pairs on mutually exclusive scf.if arms, and on A5 PIPE_V pairs the target orders itself, areexcused -- both counted and reported .

All three are read-only apart from diagnostics and off by default. They run against the existing sync path and need no new allocator.

A self-validation fixture pins that each of three fault classes is caught by exactly one gate and is silent on the other two, so no gate is redundant and none is vacuous.

Outside the new files this adds one public accessor, SyncEventIdAllocation::GetReservedEventIdNum, so the gate reads the same per-direction reservation map the sync pass obeys instead of duplicating it.


Local verification: build clean; lit 1551/1556; licence-header check passes. The 5 failures are pre-existing on unmodified main -- all under test/lit/vpto/, none referencing any flag this change adds, and this change touches no file under vpto/.

title: [Bug] [PTODSL] [阻塞] `pto.vdup` 无法处理 `ui16/ui32` 标量，生成的 operand 与 result 类型不一致
body:
### Component

Python bindings (python/)

### Description

PTODSL 的 `pto.vdup` 接口声明支持以下整数标量类型：

- `i8/i16/i32`
- `si8/si16/si32`
- `ui8/ui16/ui32`

但当输入是带类型的 `ui16` 或 `ui32` 标量时，PTODSL 生成的 `pto.vdup` operand 保留 unsigned 类型，而 result vector 被规范化为 signless integer，导致 MLIR verifier 报错：

```text
'pto.vdup' op scalar input must match result element type

### Reproduction (minimal)

```markdown
from ptodsl import pto


@pto.jit(
    name="vdup_ui16_repro",
    kernel_kind="vector",
    target="a5",
    mode="explicit",
)
def vdup_ui16_repro():
    mask = pto.pset_b16("PAT_ALL")
    pto.vdup(pto.const(32512, dtype=pto.ui16), mask)


@pto.jit(
    name="vdup_ui32_repro",
    kernel_kind="vector",
    target="a5",
    mode="explicit",
)
def vdup_ui32_repro():
    mask = pto.pset_b32("PAT_ALL")
    pto.vdup(pto.const(2147483648, dtype=pto.ui32), mask)


for name, kernel in (
    ("vdup_ui16_repro", vdup_ui16_repro),
    ("vdup_ui32_repro", vdup_ui32_repro),
):
    print(f"=== {name} ===")
    try:
        kernel.compile()
        print("PASS")
    except Exception as exc:
        print(type(exc).__name__)
        print(exc)
```

### Expected behavior

pto.vdup 应能接受其接口声明支持的 ui8/ui16/ui32 标量。
由于 PTO integer vreg 的元素类型使用 signless integer，PTODSL 应在构造 VdupOp 前，将带 signedness 的整数标量规范化为相同位宽的 signless integer，同时保持原始位模式。
例如：
```text
ui16 -> i16
ui32 -> i32
```
转换后，pto.vdup 的 scalar operand 和 result element type 应完全一致。

### Actual behavior / error logs

```text
=== vdup_ui16_repro ===
MLIRError
Verification failed:
error: unknown: 'pto.vdup' op scalar input must match result element type
 note: unknown: see current operation:
 %4 = "pto.vdup"(%2, %0)
     : (ui16, !pto.mask<b16>) -> !pto.vreg<128xi16>

=== vdup_ui32_repro ===
MLIRError
Verification failed:
error: unknown: 'pto.vdup' op scalar input must match result element type
 note: unknown: see current operation:
 %4 = "pto.vdup"(%2, %0)
     : (ui32, !pto.mask<b32>) -> !pto.vreg<64xi32>
```

title: feat(tilelib): materialize PTODSL in process
body:
## 背景

TileOp 展开此前通过独立 Python daemon 完成 PTODSL 模板选择和 MLIR 生成，需要维护子进程、Unix socket、JSON wire protocol、临时文件以及 MLIR 文本打印/解析。主线移除 legacy TileLang backend 后，这套隔离层只剩 PTODSL 使用，也阻碍了模板实例化直接复用当前编译的 MLIRContext。

## 主要变更

- 删除 TileLib daemon manager、Python socket/client/helper/wire 实现、daemon 专用测试和相关 CLI/环境配置。
- 新增与 Python 无关的 `TileLibService` C++ 边界：候选查询只传 specialization metadata，模板实例化接收当前 `MLIRContext` 并返回同 context 下的 source module handle。
- `_core` 模块初始化时安装进程级唯一 `TileLibRuntime` service；runtime 不绑定某个 compilation context，也不在 pass 中保存 Python 对象。
- 每次 `_core.main` 创建独立 Python `Context` owner，native `PTOASContext` 在该调用的动态范围内借用同一个底层 `MLIRContext`；连续多次编译共享 runtime，但 context 相互独立。
- Python callback 通过 MLIR C API capsule 找回当前 context 的 Python wrapper，在显式传入的 context 中 materialize PTODSL module；禁止 compiler path 隐式创建新 context，并校验返回 module 的 context identity。
- C++ 在 Python module owner 存活期间只借用 source module，按 entry symbol clone 所需函数及 helper 到 caller module；不转移 Python module ownership，也不走 MLIR 文本或 bytecode往返。
- `InsertTemplateAttributes` / `ExpandTileOp` 恢复为 TableGen 标准注册、默认可构造的 pass。pass 从 `getContext()` 获取当前 context，并从进程级 runtime 取得 service，因此可继续留在连续 pass pipeline，也支持 targeted IR instrumentation。
- 保留主线的 `isTileLibExpandableOp` 过滤：没有可展开 TileOp 时 pass 直接返回，不要求 runtime。
- 将 standalone `.mlir_text()` 与 compiler materialization API 分开：前者创建 fresh context，后者必须调用 `build_module_in_context(context)`。
- 将 TileValue 的 valid-shape 派生值改成按需构造的临时 view，避免 surface wrapper 与 tracing/session 之间形成循环引用，无需 weakref 或主动 wrapper invalidation。
- 更新 TileLib 选择逻辑、CLI/wheel/ST 脚本、设计文档和回归测试。

## 生命周期与边界

- Python `Context` owner 负责底层 `MLIRContext` 生命周期；`PTOASContext` 和 pass 只借用当前 compilation context。
- `TileLibRuntime` 只管理 process-wide service，module teardown 时通过 capsule 注销，避免跨 DSO/CPython 生命周期留下悬挂全局对象。
- native compiler 主流程释放 GIL；同步进入 metadata/materialize callback 时 reacquire GIL，不创建额外 worker thread 或 subinterpreter。
- Python 返回的 module/operation handle 不跨 context 使用；C++ clone 完成后即可释放 Python source module wrapper。
- 本 PR 回归覆盖同一 Python 进程内的顺序重复 `_core.main`。并发 driver invocation 仍受 LLVM 全局 command-line state 限制，不在本 PR 承诺范围内。

## 验证

- `cmake --build .work/tileop-embedded-python-study/build --target PTOASPythonPackage -j4`
- `ctest --test-dir .work/tileop-embedded-python-study/build --output-on-failure -L PTODSL -j4`：25/25 通过
- `llvm-lit -sv`：以下 4 个 TileOp/VPTO 用例全部通过
  - `expand_tile_op_ptodsl_tadd.pto`
  - `expand_tile_op_ptodsl_tsub.pto`
  - `expand_tile_op_ptodsl_view_stride_cache.pto`
  - `vpto_pipeline_vmi_after_tileop_expand.pto`
- 新增 `test_ptoas_runtime.py`，验证同一进程连续两次 `_core.main` 使用不同 compilation context 且共享 process runtime，并均完成 TileOp 展开。
- `python3 -m py_compile`、`git diff --check` 通过。

构建和测试使用 LLVM/MLIR 21.1.8。

title: fix(ci): restore parallel TileLib ST and watchdog labels
body:
## 背景

PR #1028 已经将 TileLib ST 改为按 case 使用 `pytest-xdist` 并行调度，但后续 CI workflow 修改重新使用了串行 `run_tilelib_st.py` 入口。当前 154 个 case 因此共享一个 simulator 会话串行执行；最近一次串行门禁中的 `Run TileLib ST CI` 用时约 59 分钟。

同一次门禁超过 watchdog 的 90 分钟软预算后，watchdog 虽然正确识别了慢运行，却在给 PR 添加 `ci-slow` label 时因为 `GITHUB_TOKEN` 只有 pull-request read 权限而收到 403。该 job 的 `continue-on-error` 又让 Watchdog workflow 最终显示为 success，没有留下 label 或评论。

## 修改

- 恢复 TileLib ST 的 pytest 入口，使用 16 路 `pytest-xdist --dist=worksteal` 调度独立 case。
- 保留当前 `TILELIB_ST_WORKSPACE`、PTODSL Python、PTOAS 和日志路径配置。
- 将 TileLib artifact 从整个 case simulator 工作目录收敛为聚合日志、每 case 日志、退出码、复现脚本和 msprof stdout，避免并行输出产生百万级临时文件上传。
- 为慢 CI 告警 job 同时授予 `issues: write` 和 `pull-requests: write`，使 `GITHUB_TOKEN` 可以更新 PR 的 `ci-slow` label 和 Conversation 评论。
- 移除 watchdog job 的 `continue-on-error`，使 watchdog 自身的权限或脚本错误在独立 workflow 中可见；该 workflow 不是 `ci-sim` required check，不会改变原门禁结果。

## 验证

- `.github/workflows/ci_sim.yml` 和 `.github/workflows/watchdog.yml` 通过 PyYAML 解析。
- TileLib ST Python 文件通过 `py_compile`。
- 使用 CI 同款 PTODSL Python、pytest 9.1.1 和 pytest-xdist 3.8.0：154 个 case 收集成功。
- `pytest --collect-only -n 16 --dist=worksteal test/tilelib-st/test_tilelib_st.py` 通过。
- PR CI 中 154 个 TileLib ST case 全部通过，并行运行时间为 9 分 18 秒。
- 根据该次 CI 实际输出验证 artifact 收敛：上传文件从 1,101,864 个降至 616 个，约 2.6 MB。
- `git diff --check` 通过。

后续 CI 出现的 exit 143 已确认来自宿主机 OOM：PR #1105 的 TileLib simulator 与 PR #1104 的 PTOAS 编译等任务同时运行，runner 所在 tmux scope 使用 `OOMPolicy=stop`，action 子进程成为 OOM victim 后连带关闭了整个 runner。该宿主机部署问题不通过降低本 PR 的 TileLib 并行度处理。

说明：`workflow_run` 会从默认分支加载 watchdog，因此新的 PR 写权限需要在本 PR 合入后，由下一次 PR `ci-sim` 完成事件做端到端验证。

Follow-up to #1028 and #1031.

title: [Pass Bug] level3 alloc_multi_tile fan-out addresses are not constant-folded, so multi-buffer sync degrades to single-buffer
body:
## Summary

Under `--pto-level=level3`, `pto.alloc_multi_tile addr = %base` fans the base out into a
multi-address `pto.pointer_cast`, but slot k's address is emitted as an **unfolded**
`arith.addi %base, %c<k*slotBytes>` instead of a constant. Per the multi-buffer design
(`docs/designs/ptoas-multi-buffer-explicit-design.md` §5.4.1), a `pointer_cast` whose
address list contains a non-constant operand falls back to the conservative path
(`rootBuffer = addr0`, `baseAddresses = {0}`), so all slot narrowing is lost.

Consequence: at level3 the whole multi-buffer feature degrades to single-buffer sync.

- **Dynamic slot** (`%k = arith.remui %i, %c2`): no dyn event ids at all — one static
  `EVENT_ID0`, load and consume fully serialized. level2 on the same input emits two
  primed event ids + `set_flag_dyn` / `wait_flag_dyn`.
- **Constant slots** (`%mb[0]` / `%mb[1]`): *worse than not using multi-buffer* — the two
  slots are treated as one buffer, so an extra false MTE3→MTE2 WAR pair appears that two
  plain `pto.alloc_tile`s with constant addresses do not produce.

This blocks PyPTO: when PyPTO owns local-memory planning it always invokes ptoas at
`--pto-level=level3`, so today adopting `alloc_multi_tile` / `multi_tile_get` there is a
net regression, and the feature is only usable via the ptoas memory planner (level2).

## Pass / pipeline name

`pto-view-to-memref` (level3 explicit-addr fan-out); observable in `pto-insert-sync` and
the graph sync solver.

## Command line

```bash
# dynamic slot
ptoas mb_l3.pto -o mb_l3.cpp --enable-insert-sync --pto-level=level3 --pto-arch=a3
ptoas mb_l2.pto -o mb_l2.cpp --enable-insert-sync --pto-level=level2 --pto-arch=a3  # reference

# constant slots
ptoas cs_multi_l3.pto -o cs_multi_l3.cpp --enable-insert-sync --pto-level=level3 --pto-arch=a3
ptoas cs_plain_l3.pto -o cs_plain_l3.cpp --enable-insert-sync --pto-level=level3 --pto-arch=a3  # reference
```

`--enable-graph-sync-solver` instead of `--enable-insert-sync` behaves the same.

## Before IR (input)

### A. Dynamic slot, level3 (`mb_l3.pto`)

```mlir
module {
  func.func @prefetch_dyn_eid_l3(
      %gm : memref<16x16xf16, #pto.address_space<gm>>,
      %dst : memref<16x16xf16, #pto.address_space<gm>>,
      %n : index) attributes {pto.entry} {
    %c0 = arith.constant 0 : index
    %c1 = arith.constant 1 : index
    %c2 = arith.constant 2 : index
    %base = arith.constant 32768 : i64

    %mb = pto.alloc_multi_tile addr = %base
        : !pto.multi_tile_buf<vec, 16x16xf16, count=2>

    scf.for %i = %c0 to %n step %c1 {
      %idx = arith.remui %i, %c2 : index
      %prod = pto.multi_tile_get %mb[%idx]
          : !pto.multi_tile_buf<vec, 16x16xf16, count=2>
         -> !pto.tile_buf<vec, 16x16xf16>
      pto.tload ins(%gm : memref<16x16xf16, #pto.address_space<gm>>)
                outs(%prod : !pto.tile_buf<vec, 16x16xf16>)
      pto.tstore ins(%prod : !pto.tile_buf<vec, 16x16xf16>)
                 outs(%dst : memref<16x16xf16, #pto.address_space<gm>>)
    }
    return
  }
}
```

The level2 reference (`mb_l2.pto`) is the same module with `addr = %base` and the `%base`
constant removed.

### B. Constant slots, level3 (`cs_multi_l3.pto`)

```mlir
module {
  func.func @cs_multi(%gm0 : memref<16x16xf16, #pto.address_space<gm>>,
                      %gm1 : memref<16x16xf16, #pto.address_space<gm>>,
                      %dst : memref<16x16xf16, #pto.address_space<gm>>) attributes {pto.entry} {
    %c0 = arith.constant 0 : index
    %c1 = arith.constant 1 : index
    %base = arith.constant 32768 : i64
    %mb = pto.alloc_multi_tile addr = %base : !pto.multi_tile_buf<vec, 16x16xf16, count=2>
    %s0 = pto.multi_tile_get %mb[%c0] : !pto.multi_tile_buf<vec, 16x16xf16, count=2> -> !pto.tile_buf<vec, 16x16xf16>
    %s1 = pto.multi_tile_get %mb[%c1] : !pto.multi_tile_buf<vec, 16x16xf16, count=2> -> !pto.tile_buf<vec, 16x16xf16>
    pto.tload  ins(%gm0 : memref<16x16xf16, #pto.address_space<gm>>) outs(%s0 : !pto.tile_buf<vec, 16x16xf16>)
    pto.tstore ins(%s0 : !pto.tile_buf<vec, 16x16xf16>) outs(%dst : memref<16x16xf16, #pto.address_space<gm>>)
    pto.tload  ins(%gm1 : memref<16x16xf16, #pto.address_space<gm>>) outs(%s1 : !pto.tile_buf<vec, 16x16xf16>)
    pto.tstore ins(%s1 : !pto.tile_buf<vec, 16x16xf16>) outs(%dst : memref<16x16xf16, #pto.address_space<gm>>)
    return
  }
}
```

The reference (`cs_plain_l3.pto`) replaces the multi-buffer with two plain allocs:

```mlir
    %a0 = arith.constant 32768 : i64
    %a1 = arith.constant 33280 : i64
    %s0 = pto.alloc_tile addr = %a0 : !pto.tile_buf<vec, 16x16xf16>
    %s1 = pto.alloc_tile addr = %a1 : !pto.tile_buf<vec, 16x16xf16>
```

## Expected behavior

level3 should reach the same sync quality as level2 for the same slot expressions — the
slot addresses are compile-time constants in both cases, the only difference is who
computed them.

- Case A: two primed event ids + `set_flag_dyn` / `wait_flag_dyn` keyed off the slot SSA
  (as `test/lit/pto/multi_tile_prefetch_dyn_event_id.pto` checks at the default level).
- Case B: slots 0 and 1 have disjoint `baseAddresses`, so no sync between them — the same
  sequence the two-plain-`alloc_tile` reference produces.

## Actual IR or error

IR after `pto-view-to-memref` at level3 (case A) — slot 1's address is an unfolded `addi`:

```text
%c32768_i64 = arith.constant 32768 : i64
%c512_i64 = arith.constant 512 : i64
%0 = arith.addi %c32768_i64, %c512_i64 : i64
%1 = pto.pointer_cast(%c32768_i64, %0) %c16, %c16_0 {config = ...} : memref<16x16xf16, ...>
%2 = pto.bind_tile %1, ...
scf.for %arg3 = %c0 to %arg2 step %c1 {
  %3 = arith.remui %arg3, %c2 : index
  %4 = pto.slot_marker %2[%3] : ...
  ...
}
```

Emitted C++, case A at **level3** (single static event id, serialized):

```text
set_flag(PIPE_MTE3, PIPE_MTE2, EVENT_ID0);
  wait_flag(PIPE_MTE3, PIPE_MTE2, EVENT_ID0);
  set_flag(PIPE_MTE2, PIPE_MTE3, EVENT_ID0);
  wait_flag(PIPE_MTE2, PIPE_MTE3, EVENT_ID0);
  set_flag(PIPE_MTE3, PIPE_MTE2, EVENT_ID0);
wait_flag(PIPE_MTE3, PIPE_MTE2, EVENT_ID0);
```

Same module at **level2** (correct — two event ids, dynamic ids `v14` / `v21`):

```text
set_flag(PIPE_MTE3, PIPE_MTE2, EVENT_ID0);
set_flag(PIPE_MTE3, PIPE_MTE2, EVENT_ID1);
  wait_flag(PIPE_MTE3, PIPE_MTE2, v14);
  set_flag(PIPE_MTE2, PIPE_MTE3, EVENT_ID0);
  wait_flag(PIPE_MTE2, PIPE_MTE3, EVENT_ID0);
  set_flag(PIPE_MTE3, PIPE_MTE2, v21);
wait_flag(PIPE_MTE3, PIPE_MTE2, EVENT_ID0);
wait_flag(PIPE_MTE3, PIPE_MTE2, EVENT_ID1);
```

Case B at level3 — diff of the sync/op sequence, `cs_plain_l3.cpp` → `cs_multi_l3.cpp`.
The multi-buffer version has one *extra* false WAR pair between slot 0's store and
slot 1's load:

```text
> set_flag(PIPE_MTE3, PIPE_MTE2, EVENT_ID0);
> wait_flag(PIPE_MTE3, PIPE_MTE2, EVENT_ID0);
```

## Suggested fix

In the level3 explicit-addr path of `PTOViewToMemref`, fold `base + k * slotBytes` when
`base` is a constant (both operands are constants by construction), so the fan-out
produces N literal `arith.constant` addresses — the shape `PTOPlanMemory` already produces
at level1/level2. Alternatively, run a canonicalize/fold before the InsertSync and GSS IR
translators so `UpdatePointerCastOpMemInfo` sees constants.

A regression test could extend `test/lit/pto/multi_tile_level3_explicit_addr.pto` with a
`CHECK` that the fan-out addresses are constants, plus a level3 variant of
`multi_tile_prefetch_dyn_event_id.pto`.

## Version

`ptoas 0.54` (installed binary `/usr/local/ptoas/0.54/bin/ptoas`); local source checkout
at `4259f31e915af45ac7365aea514d2cfd6aff0103`. Reproduced identically with
`--enable-insert-sync` and `--enable-graph-sync-solver`.

- Arch: a3
- PTOAS build level: level3

title: feat(vmi): 支持 width-changing vinterpret_cast
body:
## 背景

量化场景使用 256-lane BF16 向量承载中间结果。归约阶段应先通过普通 `vcvt` 显式转换为 256-lane FP32，再执行现有的 `group=8` FP32 reduction；尾部 FP8 打包则需要将 256-lane BF16 carrier 按总 bit footprint reinterpret 为 128-lane FP32。

现有 `vinterpret_cast` surface 固定保留 lane 数，layout propagation 也把 bitcast 当作普通 same-layout op，因此无法表达这种 width-changing reinterpret。

来源问题：[`learning-chip/vmi-demo#31`](https://github.com/learning-chip/vmi-demo/pull/31) 及其中的 [`quant/remain_gap/PTOAS_ASKS.md`](https://github.com/learning-chip/vmi-demo/blob/quant_remain/quant/remain_gap/PTOAS_ASKS.md)。本 PR 完成该问题所需的 PTOAS 编译/codegen 路径；产品 8192×2048 真机结果由下游采用新写法后复测。

## 正确写法

`vcmax` 保持同类型 reduction，不使用 mixed-type `to_dtype`。BF16 累积完成后显式转换一次，scale 直接从 group slots 广播回 256 lanes；FP8 打包前的 reinterpret 按总 bit footprint 改变 lane 数：

```python
amax_bf16 = ...  # 256-lane BF16 accumulation
amax_f32 = pto.vmi.vcvt(amax_bf16, to_dtype=pto.f32)
mask_f32 = pto.vmi.create_mask(256, size=256)
amax = pto.vmi.vcmax(amax_f32, mask_f32, group=8)

scale_bf16 = ...  # 8 BF16 group slots
scale_256 = pto.vmi.vbrc(scale_bf16, group=8)
quant_bf16 = pto.vmi.vmul(source_bf16, scale_256, mask_bf16)

low_bf16, high_bf16 = pto.vmi.vintlv(zero_bf16, quant_bf16, mask_bf16)
low_f32 = pto.vmi.vinterpret_cast(low_bf16, to_dtype=pto.f32)
high_f32 = pto.vmi.vinterpret_cast(high_bf16, to_dtype=pto.f32)
```

对应逻辑类型为：

```text
256xbf16 -> vcvt -> 256xf32 -> vcmax(group=8) -> 8xf32
8xbf16   -> vbrc(group=8) -> 256xbf16
256xbf16 -> vinterpret_cast -> 128xf32
```

## 修改内容

- 让 `pto.vmi.vinterpret_cast` 按总 bit footprint 推导目标 lane 数，即 `source_lanes * source_bits / target_bits`，并在结果不整除时给出诊断。
- 为 bitcast 增加独立的 layout transfer，通过表驱动声明 width-changing bitcast 当前支持 contiguous layout；必要时由 layout assignment 插入 `ensure_layout`。
- 在 `test/lit/vmi_new/opt/per_block_bf16_group8_quant_vmi_opt.pto` 增加完整优化监控：既检查 layout assignment 的 256-lane/group=8 传播，也检查端到端 VPTO 的 reduction、寄存器广播、carrier reinterpret 和 PK4 store 指令形态。
- 更新 PTODSL 用户文档与类型诊断测试。

本 PR **不** 给 `vcmax` 增加 `to_dtype`，也不新增 BF16 输入、FP32 输出的 mixed-type verifier 或专用 reduction lowering。类型转换在 surface 上保持显式。

## Codegen

显式转换后的 group=8 reduction 使用现有通用路径，生成：

```text
4 x vcvt    128xbf16 -> 64xf32 (EVEN/ODD)
3 x vmax    合并四个物理 FP32 chunk
1 x vcgmax  完成 group=8 reduction
1 x vpack + 1 x vselr  将 8 个 scale slots 在寄存器中广播
2 x vmul    对两个 BF16 物理向量执行量化乘法
3 x vintlv + 4 x vbitcast + 4 x P0 vcvt + 4 x PK4_B32 vsts
```

监控同时禁止 `vdintlv`、`vsldb`、`vsstb`、`vcmax`、额外的上述关键指令以及任何残留 VMI op/type，避免 case 只验证“能 lower”却漏掉性能形态退化。

公平 `PK4_B32` CA-model 对比中，CCE 为 32144 cycles；本 PR 的显式 final-cast VMI 路径为 31502 cycles，VMI 快 642 cycles（约 2.0%）。原 carrier reinterpret 专用路径为 31659 cycles；显式转换路径还可再减少 157 cycles。随机 BF16 输入的 FP8 与 scale 输出完全一致。

## 支持边界

- width-changing `vinterpret_cast` 必须保持总 bit footprint。
- 当前 layout 表仅声明 contiguous carrier reinterpret；其他输入 layout 由 assignment 转为 contiguous，无法合法转换时仍会报错。
- group=8 reduction 继续使用现有同类型语义；本 PR 不扩大 reduction 的 dtype 组合。

## 验证

```text
cmake --build build-main-llvm21 -j16 --target pto-test-opt
  passed

Focused VMI lit
  vmi_layout_assignment_vintlv_width_changing_bitcast: passed
  per_block_bf16_group8_quant_vmi_opt (layout assignment): passed
  per_block_bf16_group8_quant_vmi_opt (end-to-end VPTO): passed

PTODSL
  ptodsl_jit_diagnostics: passed
  ptodsl_vmi_bf16_group8_carrier: passed

git diff --check
  passed
```

完整 lit 在当前 build tree 中仍被既有 `ptoas` Python wrapper 导入错误阻塞，失败统一为 `ImportError: dynamic module does not define module export function (PyInit_ptoas)`；本 PR 直接覆盖的 `pto-test-opt` 与 PTODSL 聚焦测试均通过。

title: Add MSCATTER
[Bug] a5/level3: results regress v0.48 → v0.54 with zero arithmetic-opcode change — auto-sync flag pairs drop at v0.49, dcci scope goes OUT→ALL at v0.50
body:
## Background

DeepSeek V4-Pro is a set of 35 runnable model/test cases in `hw-native-sys/pypto-lib`
(`models/deepseek/v4-pro/`) — 27 single-card, 8 multi-card/level3 — targeting Ascend 950 (a5).
A full build of the workload emits 3285 `.pto` files, 473 uniquely named. Throughout this
report, **"case"** means a runnable `.py` and **"kernel"** means one of the 473 `.pto` units.

We are trying to move that workload from PTOAS **v0.48** to **v0.54**, so that we can also take
current `pypto` main, whose relanded `InsertCommFence` pass emits `pto.cmo.cacheinvalid` /
`pto.fence.barrier_all` (ops v0.48 does not know — see the MoE compile failure below).

We ran a full 2×2 (two pypto revisions × two PTOAS binaries) to check whether this is PTOAS or
our own compiler. It is PTOAS.

**Reproduction environment** (the tree that reproduces; nothing reset to latest main):

| Component | Version |
|---|---|
| pypto-lib | `fd91568` (branch `main`, on `origin/main`) |
| pypto | `a8ef572f` (branch `main`) — also tested at `a20e884f` (current main) |
| simpler | `8e00319e` (detached) **+ a local 31-line uncommitted patch** to `src/a5/platform/onboard/host/aicpu_topology_probe.cpp` (host CPU-topology probe fallback; identical in all four arms) |
| pto-isa | `83d01313` (detached) |
| ptoas | **v0.48** (working) vs **v0.54** (regressing) |
| CANN | 9.1.0-beta.3 |
| driver | 25.7.rc1.6 |
| host | Linux x86_64 |
| target | a5, `--pto-level=level3`, PYPTO memory planner |

Repro cases: `models/deepseek/v4-pro/{gate,hc_pre,prefill_compressor_ratio4,decode_attention_csa}.py`
at pypto-lib `fd91568`. All four, and every file on their import graphs, are committed and
unmodified in the tree that produced these results. (The one dirty file in that directory,
`moe.py`, is not on any of the four import graphs.)

**Diagnosis: `ptoas`** — the 2×2 holds pypto, pypto-lib, simpler, pto-isa, CANN, driver and
hardware fixed and moves only the PTOAS binary; 12/12 PASS on v0.48 and 0/12 on v0.54 in both
pypto arms.

---

## Description

On **four single-card cases** (of a 27-case single-card suite), moving PTOAS v0.48 → v0.54 takes
us from **12/12 PASS to 0/12 PASS** on real a5 hardware at `--pto-level=level3`, with **zero
arithmetic-opcode changes** anywhere in the generated code. The failures are memory-ordering /
cache-coherency shaped (NaN, wrong results, a VEC-UB-out-of-bounds device fault), not numerical.

These four cases were selected because they failed a first v0.54 smoke sweep. They are not a
random sample. Scope of the on-device result: a5, `--pto-level=level3`, PYPTO memory planner,
one card, one session. We did not test `--pto-level=level2` or other targets on device.

### Honest baseline: v0.48 is *mostly* stable, with two known exceptions that are ours

We want to disclose this up front rather than have you find it:

- **`prefill_attention_csa` already faults on v0.48**, at a 25–44 % rate (5/20 and 7/16 in our
  2026-07-31 sweep), with `errcode:(341) The address for VEC to access UB is out of bounds` —
  the *same* error code we report below for `decode_attention_csa` on v0.54. It is tracked as
  our own open bug, `hw-native-sys/pypto-lib#858`, with no root cause and no kernel-level fix.
  **We are not attributing #858 to PTOAS.**
- **`qkv_proj_rope` is flaky on v0.48** in this session: 3 of 7 runs FAIL on output `q`, at error ratios 0.90 %, 1.19 % and 1.26 % against a 0.50 % budget.

Neither of those two cases is in the 2×2 below. Excluding them, a 23-case single-card sweep on
v0.48 in this session is 22/23 PASS (the one failure is `qkv_proj_rope`).

### The PTOAS binary is the only variable we changed — full 2×2

Four single-card cases (`gate`, `hc_pre`, `prefill_compressor_ratio4`, `decode_attention_csa`),
3 repetitions each, **run strictly serially** (one JIT build in the tree at a time, so no build
contention), on real a5 hardware.

| | ptoas v0.48 | ptoas v0.54 |
|---|---|---|
| pypto `a8ef572f` | **12/12 PASS** | **0/12 PASS** |
| pypto `a20e884f` (current main) | **12/12 PASS** | **0/12 PASS** |

24 PASS on v0.48, 24 FAIL on v0.54, no crossover. (We are deliberately not quoting a p-value:
these are 4 cases × 3 repetitions, not 24 independent draws.)

The only variables between the two ptoas arms are `PTOAS_ROOT` and the matching
`LD_LIBRARY_PATH` needed to load that build's shared libraries. Nothing in pypto, pypto-lib,
simpler, pto-isa, CANN, the driver or the hardware changes.

**On the pypto axis.** The `.pto` that current-main pypto feeds to PTOAS differs from the older
pypto's by SSA/inline-counter renaming *plus* a set of newly emitted `arith.maxsi <offset>, 0`
partition-view offset clamps (30 across the `gate` case, 422 across `decode_attention_csa`'s 47
kernels; `a8ef572f` emits none). That is a real added op, not just renumbering. What matters
here is that it carries **no memory-ordering content**: both revisions' `.pto` for all four
failing cases contain **zero** `pto.fence.*` and **zero** `pto.cmo.*`. The pypto axis is inert
in outcome — both rows are 12/12 on v0.48 and 0/12 on v0.54.

### Per-case failures on v0.54 (3/3 reproducible each)

| Case | Failure |
|---|---|
| `decode_attention_csa` | `errcode:(341) The address for VEC to access UB is out of bounds` |
| `hc_pre` | output `comb` returns `NaN=64` of 128 elements |
| `gate` | output `weights` mismatches golden (3/3); `indices` also mismatches (2/3) |
| `prefill_compressor_ratio4` | output `cmp_kv` mismatches golden (this case has a **zero** error budget, `max_error_ratio=0.0`) |

The failures reproduce 3/3 in every v0.54 arm and are per-repetition identical across the two
pypto revisions. The corruption itself is **not** bit-deterministic:
`prefill_compressor_ratio4`'s error count varies 1793–1811 of 2097152 across repetitions, and
`gate` repetition 2 mismatches `weights` alone while repetitions 1 and 3 mismatch `indices` and
`weights` — the same pattern in both pypto arms. Run-to-run variation of this shape is what we
would expect from a memory-ordering change rather than a numerics change.

`decode_attention_csa` is our sharpest signal: it has a **20/20 clean** record on v0.48 from our
2026-07-31 sweep (at pypto-lib `d9b5fef`, a different pypto-lib revision from this report's
`fd91568`), and in this session at `fd91568` it was **6/6 PASS on v0.48** (3 reps × 2 pypto
arms) and **3/3 device-fault on v0.54**.

### Breadth (weaker evidence, included so you can bound the blast radius)

A single-repetition v0.54 sweep over 26 single-card cases, run in parallel rather than in the
serial harness, gives **11 PASS / 15 FAIL**, with **9 distinct cases** hitting `errcode:(341)`
(`decode_attention_csa`, `decode_attention_hca`, `decode_attention_swa`, `decode_indexer`,
`prefill_attention_csa`, `prefill_attention_hca`, `prefill_attention_swa`, `prefill_indexer`,
`qkv_proj_rope`). We do not treat this as a gate — one run per case, parallel builds, and two of
those cases are the known-flaky ones above — but it indicates the effect is not confined to the
four cases in the 2×2, and that 11 cases still pass on v0.54.

### The alternative reading we cannot rule out

It is possible that v0.54's sync/CMO scheduling is **legal** and is merely exposing a latent
memory-ordering bug in our kernels. We take that seriously precisely because
`errcode:(341)` is an error our workload already produces on v0.48 (pypto-lib#858, open,
unattributed). We are raising it with PTOAS because (i) the change is on your side of the
boundary, (ii) the flip is 12/12 → 0/12 with nothing else varying, and (iii) we cannot
distinguish "legal change" from "incorrect change" without knowing the intended CMO/fence
contract — which is ask (2) below either way.

What would distinguish the two readings: if the removed `set_flag`/`wait_flag` pairs at the sites
below are ones the new pass model can *prove* redundant, this is ours; if the pass is relying on
an ordering guarantee that the emitted code does not actually establish, it is yours. That is a
question about your dependence model that we cannot answer from the outside.

---

## Reproduction (minimal)

### 0. Standalone emission repro — 13 lines of PTO, no hardware, no corpus

Save as `min.pto`. This is the unmodified `.pto` our compiler emits for the
`prefill_swa_dummy_cmp_table` kernel of `models/deepseek/v4-pro/prefill_attention_swa.py` (693
bytes), chosen because it is the smallest kernel in the workload that still exhibits the change:

```mlir
module attributes {pto.target_arch = "a5"} {
  func.func @prefill_swa_dummy_cmp_table(%arg0: !pto.ptr<i32>) attributes {pto.kernel_kind = #pto.kernel_kind<vector>} {
  %c32_index = arith.constant 32 : index
  %c1_index = arith.constant 1 : index
  %c0_index = arith.constant 0 : index
  %cmp_block_table_dummy_inline548__ssa_v0_view = pto.make_tensor_view %arg0, shape = [%c32_index], strides = [%c1_index] {layout = #pto.layout<nd>}: !pto.tensor_view<?xi32>
  scf.for %dummy_blk_inline519__idx_v0 = %c0_index to %c32_index step %c1_index {
    %0 = arith.index_cast %c0_index : index to i32
    pto.store_scalar %0, %arg0[%dummy_blk_inline519__idx_v0] : !pto.ptr<i32>, i32
  }
  return
  }
}
```

```bash
ptoas min.pto -o min.cpp --enable-insert-sync --pto-level=level3 --pto-arch a5
```

(These are exactly the flags pypto uses in production — `_get_ptoas_flags` in
`pypto/python/pypto/backend/pto_backend.py`, plus the a5 handler's `--pto-arch a5`.)

Complete diff of the emitted C++ (v0.48 = 45 lines, v0.54 = 50 lines), rc=0 in both:

```diff
@@ -20,6 +20,11 @@
   }
 }
 
+template <typename Ptr>
+static AICORE inline void PTOAS__DCCI_SINGLE_CACHE_LINE(Ptr ptr) {
+  dcci((__gm__ void*)ptr, cache_line_t::SINGLE_CACHE_LINE);
+}
+
 AICORE void prefill_swa_dummy_cmp_table(__gm__ int32_t* v1) {
@@ -30,16 +35,16 @@
   set_vector_mask(-1, -1);
-  for (size_t v6 = (size_t) v2; v6 < ((size_t) v4); v6 += (size_t) v3) {
-    v1[v6] = v5;
+  for (int64_t i6 = v2; i6 < v4; i6 += v3) {
+    v1[i6] = v5;
   }
   pipe_barrier(PIPE_ALL);
-  dcci((__gm__ void*)0, ENTIRE_DATA_CACHE, CACHELINE_OUT);
+  dcci((__gm__ void*)0, cache_line_t::ENTIRE_DATA_CACHE);
   dsb((mem_dsb_t)0);
   #endif // __DAV_VEC__
 
   pipe_barrier(PIPE_ALL);
-  dcci((__gm__ void*)0, ENTIRE_DATA_CACHE, CACHELINE_OUT);
+  dcci((__gm__ void*)0, cache_line_t::ENTIRE_DATA_CACHE);
   dsb((mem_dsb_t)0);
   ptoas_auto_sync_tail(PTOAutoSyncTailMode::kBarrierAll);
```

The `dcci` emission delta is **independent of `--pto-level` (level2, level3), `--pto-arch` (a3,
a5), and `--enable-insert-sync` (present or absent)** — verified on this kernel, all 8
combinations, rc=0 everywhere.

We picked a kernel from `prefill_attention_swa` rather than from one of the four failing cases
because the failing cases' `dcci`-bearing kernels are too large to inline: `route_sort` (`gate`)
is 24,236 B with a 373-line emitted diff and `kv_and_cache_write` (`decode_attention_csa`) is
16,348 B with a 133-line diff. The `dcci` rewrite is identical in all 33. We can attach any of
them on request.

### 1. Host-only bisect v0.48 → v0.54 — this is the most useful thing in the report

We downloaded the `ptoas-bin-x86_64.tar.gz` asset of every release v0.48…v0.54 and re-compiled
two representative kernels with each. **Neither change is a v0.54 change** — they land at
**v0.49** and **v0.50**:

| Release | `mix_x`: `set_flag` / `wait_flag` | `route_sort`: `dcci` call form |
|---|---|---|
| v0.48 | 17 / 17 | `dcci(ptr, ENTIRE_DATA_CACHE, CACHELINE_OUT)` (3-arg) |
| **v0.49** | **11 / 11** | 3-arg |
| **v0.50** | 11 / 11 | **`dcci(ptr, cache_line_t::SINGLE_CACHE_LINE)` (2-arg)** |
| v0.51 | 11 / 11 | 2-arg |
| v0.52 | 11 / 11 | 2-arg |
| v0.53 | 11 / 11 | 2-arg |
| v0.54 | 11 / 11 | 2-arg |

- `mix_x` is the kernel in the failing `hc_pre` case that loses flag pairs.
- `route_sort` is the kernel in the failing `gate` case that gains a `dcci` body call.

So the flag-pair reduction is introduced in **v0.49** and the `dcci` call-form change in
**v0.50**; v0.51–v0.54 are unchanged for both. If you want to reproduce our on-device result
with the smallest possible delta, **v0.49 and v0.50 are the releases to look at**, not v0.54.

Scope of this bisect, stated precisely: it is **two kernels**, chosen because they are the ones
implicated in two of our four failing cases. We did **not** re-run the full 473-kernel corpus at
every intermediate release, so we are not claiming per-release counts for the other 40
sync-changed / 32 `dcci`-changed kernels.

**Incidental finding on v0.50.** `csa_slots_build_valid_qk_plan.pto` (118 827 B, from
`decode_attention_csa`) **does not finish compiling on v0.50** — we killed it at 180 s, where
v0.48 takes 0.26 s and v0.54 takes 0.63 s. That is consistent with PTOAS#950, and it is why the
`dcci` column above is measured on `route_sort` rather than on that kernel. We mention it only as
confirmation that #950 was real and is fixed by v0.51+; it is not part of the regression we are
reporting.

We have **not** run a device bisect. Say the word and we will run the on-device 2×2 at v0.49 and
v0.50 and post the result.

### 2. Differential compile over the whole workload — no hardware needed

473 uniquely-named `.pto` kernels from the V4-Pro build output, compiled with each binary under
the flags above:

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| kernels compiled OK on v0.48 | 473 / 473 |
| kernels compiled OK on v0.54 | 473 / 473 |
| kernels whose emitted C++ differs | 473 / 473 — but see note |
| **kernels with a `T*` opcode-count change** | **0 / 473** |
| kernels with a `set_flag` / `wait_flag` count change | 37 / 473 (29 fewer, 8 more) |
| kernels with a `pipe_barrier` / `dsb` count change | 10 / 473 (all 10 fewer — e.g. `dispatch_push` `dsb` 1 → 0, `dispatch_meta` `pipe_barrier` 6 → 5) |
| kernels containing a `dcci` call in the kernel body — **same 33 in both versions, 66 call sites each; every site changes from the 3-arg to the 2-arg form** | 33 / 473 |
| kernels gaining a dead, never-called `PTOAS__DCCI_SINGLE_CACHE_LINE` template preamble | 473 / 473 |

Note on the "473/473 differ" row: the reason it is 473 and not ~50 is the unconditional
`PTOAS__DCCI_SINGLE_CACHE_LINE` template preamble, which v0.54 emits into every file and calls in
none of them (0 call sites across all 473). The substantive deltas are the rows below it.

Note for anyone re-deriving the `dcci` numbers: a raw `grep -c dcci` shows a delta on 473/473 for
that same reason. **No kernel gains or loses a real `dcci` call site** — `grep -h 'dcci((__gm__
void\*)0' out48/*.cpp | sort | uniq -c` gives 66 × the 3-arg form, and the same command on
`out54` gives 66 × the 2-arg form, over an identical set of 33 files.

Method for the arithmetic row: for each of the 473 kernels we counted every `T*` tile intrinsic
appearing in either output — **52 distinct opcodes**, including `TMATMUL`, `TMATMUL_ACC`,
`TMULS`, `TADDS`, `TROWSUM`, `TROWEXPANDMUL`, `TSQRT`, `TSORT32`, `TMRGSORT` — after stripping
comments and `[[pto::last_use(...)]]` attributes. Per-kernel opcode multisets are identical in
473/473. **Caveat:** this compares opcode *counts*, not instruction order, operands, tile shapes
or dtypes. It rules out a numerics *rewrite*; it does not rule out a reordering. The remaining
diffs are confined to `set_flag`/`wait_flag`, `pipe_barrier`/`dsb`, and `dcci`.

### 3. The `dcci` change, stated precisely

```c
// ptoas v0.48 — lines 1546 / 1551 of the emitted C++ for csa_slots_build_valid_qk_plan.pto (118,827 B)
dcci((__gm__ void*)0, ENTIRE_DATA_CACHE, CACHELINE_OUT);

// ptoas v0.54 — lines 2369 / 2374 of the same kernel
dcci((__gm__ void*)0, cache_line_t::ENTIRE_DATA_CACHE);
```

Per CANN 9.1.0-beta.3, `tools/bisheng_compiler/lib/clang/15.0.5/include/`:

- `cce_aicore_intrinsics.h`, `cache_line_t` (lines 285–290): `SINGLE_CACHE_LINE = 0`, `ENTIRE_DATA_CACHE = 1`
- `cce_aicore_intrinsics.h`, `dcci_dst_t` (lines 299–310): `CACHELINE_ALL = 0`, `CACHELINE_OUT = 2`
  (`CACHELINE_UB` is `#if`-excluded when `__NPU_ARCH__` is 3510 **or** 3801; `ccec -dM -E
  --cce-aicore-arch=dav-c310-vec` predefines `__NPU_ARCH__ 3510`, i.e. a5)
- `__clang_cce_simt_dav3510_intrinsic.h:70`:
  `dcci(__gm__ void *dst, uint64_t entire, uint64_t type = 0)` — **the 2-argument form defaults
  `type = 0 = CACHELINE_ALL`.**

Confirmed in the device object: compiling the three spellings with
`ccec -c -O3 -x cce -std=c++17 --cce-aicore-only --cce-aicore-arch=dav-c310-vec` and dumping
`.text`, the 3-arg `CACHELINE_OUT` form encodes as `02002e40`, the 3-arg `CACHELINE_ALL` form as
`00002e40`, and the 2-arg form as `00002e40` — byte-identical to `CACHELINE_ALL`.

**So the invalidate scope went from `OUT` to `ALL`, i.e. it got *wider*, not narrower.** We are
therefore explicitly **not** claiming this alone explains the failures. We flag it because it is
an unannounced semantic change at 66 call sites across 33 of the 473 kernels, and we would like
to know whether it was intended. See the mechanism ranking below.

Both versions' emitted C++ compiles cleanly for the device. We did not device-compile all 473;
we device-compiled `csa_slots_build_valid_qk_plan` and the minimal kernel above from both trees,
rc=0 in all four, with the full production flag set:

```bash
ccec -c -O3 -x cce -std=c++17 --cce-aicore-only --cce-aicore-arch=dav-c310-vec \
  -mllvm -cce-aicore-stack-size=0x8000 -mllvm -cce-aicore-function-stack-size=0x8000 \
  -mllvm -cce-aicore-record-overflow=false -mllvm -cce-aicore-addr-transform \
  -mllvm -cce-aicore-dcci-insert-for-scalar=false -mllvm -cce-vf-aa-between-iters=true \
  -DMEMORY_BASE -I<pto-isa>/include -I<pto-isa>/include/pto -I<pypto>/runtime/simpler_setup/incore
```

(The bare `ccec -c -O3 -x cce ...` line without those includes fails on
`'pto/pto-inst.hpp' file not found` — please use the full command.) Note
`-mllvm -cce-aicore-dcci-insert-for-scalar=false` is in our production set, which is directly
relevant to the `dcci` story: we rely on PTOAS, not the backend, to place these.

### 4. Correlation with the observed failures — and the counter-examples

All four failing cases own at least one changed kernel:

| Failing case | `dcci`-form-changed kernels it owns | Flag/barrier-changed kernels it owns |
|---|---|---|
| `gate` | `route_sort` | — |
| `decode_attention_csa` | `csa_slots_build_valid_qk_plan`, `kv_and_cache_write` | `mix_x` 17→11, `rmsnorm_rope_cache_write` 41→40, `rmsnorm_rope` 22→21, `weights_proj_reduce` 13→3 |
| `hc_pre` | — | `mix_x` 17→11 (six fewer flag pairs) |
| `prefill_compressor_ratio4` | — | `prefill_c4_rmsnorm_rope` 26→25 |

**Counter-examples exist in both directions, and we would rather show them than have you find
them.** `decode_sparse_attn` owns `csa_slots_build_valid_qk_plan` — a `dcci`-changed kernel — and
**passes** on v0.54. `qkv_proj_rope` **fails** on v0.54 with no `dcci` change and no flag/barrier
change at all (it is also 4/8 flaky on v0.48, so we weight it lightly). We present this table as
a lead worth checking, not as a strong correlation and certainly not as a proven root cause.

### 5. Which mechanism we would look at first

We think the **sync-scheduling change is the stronger candidate**, and we would rank it above the
`dcci` change:

1. **Auto-sync flag scheduling, landing at v0.49.** `hc_pre` fails with `NaN=64` and its `mix_x`
   kernel has *no* `dcci` change of any kind — its only substantive delta is six fewer
   `set_flag`/`wait_flag` pairs (17→11), and that delta lands at v0.49. So `dcci` cannot explain
   at least one of the four failures, while a sync-scheduling change can explain all four.
   `weights_proj_reduce` 13→3 in `decode_attention_csa` is the largest single reduction.
2. **The `dcci` destination-scope change, landing at v0.50.** Ranked second precisely because
   `OUT` → `ALL` is a *widening*, which is a weak story for stale data. We still want to know if
   it was deliberate.

We do not name a specific PR: we checked the obvious candidates and the merge dates do not line
up. #953 ("Remove automatic memory consistency pass", merged 2026-07-17) is in v0.50…v0.51;
#1001, #951, #1007 and #1011 all merged 2026-07-27/28, i.e. v0.52 and v0.53. Our bisect puts
both emission changes at **v0.49 and v0.50**, before all of those. You will know your own history
better than we can reconstruct it from tag dates.

### 6. Why we cannot simply stay on v0.48, and why the contract question matters

Current-main pypto's relanded `InsertCommFence` emits ops v0.48 cannot parse. The multi-card MoE
build on v0.48 fails outright:

```text
Failed to compile function 'dispatch_push': ptoas compilation failed:
  loc(".../ptoas/dispatch_push.pto":69:9): error: custom op 'pto.cmo.cacheinvalid' is unknown
Error: Failed to parse MLIR.
```

— for five functions (`combine`, `combine_wait`, `dispatch_meta`, `dispatch_push`,
`dispatch_wait`). So once we take current pypto, staying on v0.48 is not an option for us.

That same log also shows `InsertCommFence` **does** fire on the distributed/publish path. It does
not fire for our four single-card cases. `IsPublishingWrite`
(`pypto@a20e884f:src/ir/transforms/utils/op_predicates.cpp:77`) fires only on `pld.*` remote
writes; on a `tile.store` / `tensor.write` / `pld.tile.get` / `pld.tensor.get` whose destination
is a `DistributedTensorType`; or on a conservative fallback for unregistered ops, i.e. user
function calls. These four cases are single-core and non-distributed, so no DistributedTensor
trigger applies, and there are **0 `func.call` across all 473 `.pto`**, so the fallback is dead
too. Empirically: the `.pto` emitted by `a20e884f` for all four failing cases contains **zero**
`pto.fence.*` and **zero** `pto.cmo.*`. PTOAS no longer inserts on this path, and pypto does not
either.

(Correction to a claim we nearly made: `pl.submit` is unused anywhere in this workload, but
`decode_attention_csa` *does* enter one `pl.manual_scope`, via
`decode_sparse_attn.sparse_attn` at `decode_sparse_attn.py:487`. It still emits no fence and no
CMO. Corroborating this: the four cases in the workload that use `pl.manual_scope` —
`decode_sparse_attn{,_hca,_swa}`, `prefill_sparse_attn` — all **pass** on v0.54.)

### 7. Device reproduction (needs a5)

```bash
git clone https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto-lib && git -C pypto-lib checkout fd91568
git clone https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto     && git -C pypto     checkout a8ef572f
git -C pypto submodule update --init runtime          # simpler 8e00319e
# CANN 9.1.0-beta.3 sourced; PYTHONPATH=<pypto>/python:<pypto>/runtime/python:<pypto-lib>

export PTOAS_ROOT=/path/to/ptoas-v0.48        # dir containing ./ptoas (or ./bin/ptoas)
cd pypto-lib/models/deepseek/v4-pro
for c in gate hc_pre prefill_compressor_ratio4 decode_attention_csa; do
  for i in 1 2 3; do python $c.py -p a5 -d 0; done    # expect 12/12 PASS
done

export PTOAS_ROOT=/path/to/ptoas-v0.54/bin
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/path/to/ptoas-v0.54/lib:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH
# repeat the same loop                                 # observed 0/12
```

Run the loop **serially** — one JIT build in the tree at a time. Note that
`pypto/toolchain/versions.env` is CI-only and is never consulted at runtime: pypto resolves the
binary purely from `PTOAS_ROOT` (`$PTOAS_ROOT/ptoas`, falling back to `$PTOAS_ROOT/bin/ptoas` for
the v0.51+ layout) and never probes `--version`. Swapping `versions.env` will change nothing.

The 473-kernel `.pto` corpus is generated build output and is not committed anywhere. To
regenerate it, run each case once under the setup above — every run leaves its kernels in
`build_output/_jit_<case>_<timestamp>/ptoas/*.pto`, and `run_jit(..., compile_only=True)` in
`golden/runner.py` gets you the `.pto` with no device. We have the 473-file corpus and all
emitted-C++ trees (v0.48/v0.49/v0.50/v0.54) archived; say the word and we will attach the tarball
to this issue via the web UI (`gh issue create` cannot upload).

---

## Expected behavior

For a workload whose arithmetic opcodes are unchanged, moving v0.48 → v0.54 should not change
results on device. Concretely, either:

1. the `dcci` destination-cache scope emitted for these kernels should be preserved, or the
   change from `CACHELINE_OUT` to the 2-argument (`CACHELINE_ALL`) form should be documented as
   intentional; and
2. if the auto-sync model legitimately proves those `set_flag`/`wait_flag` pairs redundant, and
   the CMO/fence contract has intentionally moved to the producer, that contract should be
   documented so pypto can emit the equivalent — specifically **what a frontend must now emit for
   non-distributed, single-core kernels**, not only for the cross-rank publish/wait case.

### What would help us most (three bounded asks)

1. **Was the `dcci` 3-arg → 2-arg change (v0.50) intentional?** One-line answer is enough; if
   yes, what should a producer emit to get `CACHELINE_OUT` semantics back.
2. **Was the auto-sync flag-pair reduction at v0.49 (e.g. `mix_x` 17 → 11, `weights_proj_reduce`
   13 → 3) intentional, and on what dependence model?** This is the one we cannot resolve
   ourselves, and it is what decides whether the latent-bug reading above is the right one.
3. **Tell us which on-device bisect point you want** and we will run the same serial 2×2 there.
   Our host bisect says the emission changes are at v0.49 and v0.50; v0.49 and v0.50 on device
   are the two runs we would do first unless you prefer others.

We have **not** tested **v0.55** (released 2026-08-03); this report is v0.48 vs v0.54. If you
want v0.55 data, say so and we will run the same 2×2 on it.

---

## Actual behavior / error logs

```text
decode_attention_csa (3/3):
  The extend info: errcode:(341) errorStr: The address for VEC to access UB is out of bounds.
    subErrType: 0x4.[FUNC:ProcessDavidStarsCoreErrorInfo][FILE:device_error_proc_c.cc][LINE:750]

hc_pre (3/3):
  [RUN]   'comb' FAIL  shape=(8, 16) dtype=torch.float32 (ratio_allclose(atol=2.5e-05, rtol=0.005, max_error_ratio=0.005))
  Output(s) does not match golden: ['comb']
    illegal values in actual: NaN=64 Inf=0

gate (3/3):
  Output(s) does not match golden: ['indices', 'weights']     # reps 1 and 3
  Output(s) does not match golden: ['weights']                # rep 2

prefill_compressor_ratio4 (3/3):
  [RUN]   'cmp_kv' FAIL  shape=(32, 128, 1, 512) dtype=torch.bfloat16
    (ratio_allclose(atol=0.0001, rtol=0.0078125, max_error_ratio=0.0))
    error_count=1810 / 2097152        # varies 1793-1811 across reps

multi-card MoE on v0.48 with current-main pypto (why v0.48 is not a fallback for us):
  Failed to compile function 'dispatch_push': ptoas compilation failed:
    loc(".../ptoas/dispatch_push.pto":69:9): error: custom op 'pto.cmo.cacheinvalid' is unknown
  Error: Failed to parse MLIR.
```

All four cases are PASS, 12/12, on v0.48 in the same serial harness on the same hardware in the
same session, under both pypto revisions.

---

## Git commit

We consume PTOAS as a release binary, not from source. Release-tag commits:

- **working**: `v0.48` = `a45233eef74a9e2b79494fb9cfd2f9419a5d6eaf`
  (`ptoas-bin-x86_64.tar.gz`, sha256 `701249dc3d49045814a147cd6f516f624a7d2d1a59041f1d99f3e4c637857bbe`)
- **regressing**: `v0.54` = `195fdb8c53545bf8ca1439a7e770a4a3e356d582`
  (`ptoas-bin-x86_64.tar.gz`, sha256 `4e3acb9623384c18fe264610525777210095f2ba24f6c52b9823bf1cb81d7a99`,
  which matches `PTOAS_SHA256_X86_64` in `pypto@a20e884f:toolchain/versions.env`)

Both binaries self-report `ptoas 0.48` and `ptoas 0.54`. The host-only bisect in §1 additionally
used the `ptoas-bin-x86_64.tar.gz` assets of v0.49 through v0.53.

## Component

Passes / Transforms (lib/PTO/Transforms)

*(We pick Transforms rather than EmitC because the flag-pair reduction at v0.49 is the hypothesis
we rank first — see §5. The `dcci` form change at v0.50 is an EmitC-side question and is the
second ask.)*

## Host platform

Linux (x86_64)

## Target Ascend arch

a5

## PTOAS build level

level3

title: fix(vmi): dynamic vci index + group-periodic share (raw vci)
body:
## Summary
- Dynamic loop IVs (`TileLang T.serial` / `scf.for`) arrive as MLIR `index`; coerce to signless **i32** in PTODSL so `pto.vmi.vci` ODS/verify accept the base.
- Restore optional `{group}` on `vci`/`iota` (ODS + PTODSL `group=`), preserve through unified→legacy and rematerialize.
- **Semantics:** without `{group}` → continuous ramp `base..base+L-1` (VL128: `0..63` then `64..127`). With `{group=C}` → group-periodic restart per group of size `S = L/C`.
- Contiguous packing lowers as raw **`pto.vci(%chunkBase)`**. Identical group runs share one physical index VL (`return %idx, %idx` for VL128/`g=2`).
- **Sub-VL contiguous groups** (`S < physVL` and `physVL % S == 0`, e.g. i32 `64/g=2`, i16 `128/g=2`): `vci(base)` then per-group `∓ g·S` + lane-range `vsel`. Early reject when `S` neither divides nor is a multiple of phys VL (ODS verify + PTODSL).
- **Deinterleaved / interleaved group results:** no dedicated grouped-deint iota path. Require contiguous materialization; unified→legacy rewrites non-contiguous grouped `vci`/`iota` to **contiguous iota + `ensure_layout`** so layout infer / rematerialize can produce `vdintlv` etc.

## Test plan
- [x] lit: `vmi_to_vpto_iota_group2.pto` → shared `%idx = pto.vci %base`
- [x] lit: `vmi_to_vpto_iota_group_subvl.pto` → i32 64/g2, i16 128/g2, i32 128/g4 share
- [x] lit: `vmi_to_vpto_iota_group_deint.pto` → shared contiguous `vci` then `vdintlv`
- [x] `python3 ptodsl/tests/test_vmi_vci_dynamic_index.py` (const / dynamic / group=2 / sub-VL / untileable reject)
- [x] Simple camodel share case:
  `scripts/sim_dsl.sh --output /tmp/vci_vadds_g2_out ptodsl/examples/vci_vadds_share_launch.py -- --groups 2`
  → `vci(0)+vadds(1000)+vsts` expects `1000..1063|1000..1063` (g=1: `1000..1063`)
- [ ] CI ptodsl / lit as applicable

After rebuild: `ninja ptoas_runtime_staging` (`ptoas` loads `runtime-staging/lib/ptoas.so`).

title: [VMI] Align group=4 broadcast support with group=8
body:
## 背景

#1085 中的 compact reciprocal expand 需要将 `group_slots(num_groups=4, slots=1)` 的 4 个 `f32` 标量直接扩展为 128-lane 向量，避免先写入 pad-32 UB 再以 `dist_mode="brc"` 读回。

本 PR 将 group=4 broadcast 的“元素类型 × 逻辑向量长度”支持范围补齐到 group=8 的现有矩阵。layout 仍由编译器内部选择，不作为调用侧限制。

## 改动

- 对可塑的 group-broadcast producer 优先选择 packed `slots=8` carrier，使其走单 source VReg 的 `vselr` lowering。
- 为 group=4 的 half-VReg、每组一个 VCG block 形状自动选择内部 `contiguous(lane_stride=2)` carrier，补齐：
  - `i8 × 128`
  - `i16/f16/bf16 × 64`
  - `i32/f32 × 32`
- 修正 lane-stride result 的 selector period，使 selector 与物理 lane 映射一致。
- 对必须保持 `slots=1` 的输入增加跨 source VReg 的 `vdup + vsel` 合并 lowering，覆盖 #1085 的显式 layout fixture。
- 增加显式 `slots=1` 和无显式 layout 的 shape-matrix 回归测试。

## 支持范围

经逐项探测，group=4 broadcast 已覆盖 group=8 当前支持的全部类型/逻辑长度组合：

- `i8`：64～8192 lanes
- `i16/f16/bf16`：32～4096 lanes
- `i32/f32`：16～2048 lanes

Reduce 的 `add/min/max` 未发现 group=8 可通过而 group=4 不可通过的组合；group=4 现有 reduce 能力是 group=8 的超集，因此本 PR 不修改 reduce lowering。

## 验证

- `ninja -C build-llvm21 pto-test-opt`
- 直接运行 #1085 最新 `desired_compact_vmi.pto`：通过，无残留 VMI
- 直接运行 #1085 原 `current_pad_brc_vmi.pto` workaround：通过
- group=4/group=8 broadcast 全类型长度矩阵扫描：通过
- reduce `add/min/max` 的 144 个 op/type/length 组合对比：group=4 覆盖全部 group=8 支持项
- group-broadcast lit：14/14 通过
- `vmi_new` lit：446/446 通过
- 全量 `check-pto`：1548 passed、1 unsupported、5 failed；5 项均为现有 A3 UB/soft-postupdate FileCheck 预期差异，与本 PR 无关
- `git diff --check`：通过

Related to #1085

title: [VMI] Optimize layout and predicate lowering for widen workloads
body:
## 背景

VMI widen 类 workload 中存在几类相互叠加的冗余：逻辑上连续的 group load 在 layout assignment 前仍保留分组语义；静态前缀 mask 同时生成 `pge` 和 `pset`，阻碍 CSE；1PT store 携带硬件不读取的 predicate；全真 predicate 的 interleave/deinterleave 产生多余指令；窄化后立即扩展的 cast 链也可能被较弱的 layout seed 拆开并插入额外 layout materialization。

## 关联问题

- Related to https://github.com/hw-native-sys/PTOAS/issues/1024
- 端到端复现：https://github.com/learning-chip/vmi-demo/pull/30
- 原始问题说明：https://github.com/learning-chip/vmi-demo/blob/widen_issue/quant/quant_dequant/PTOAS_ASKS.md

## 修改

- 在 VMI layout assignment 前将满足 `row_stride == lane_count / group_count` 的连续 group load 规范化为普通 load，同时保留动态或非连续 stride 的 group load。
- 将 VMI lowering 生成的静态前缀 mask 统一为 `pset`，使等价静态 mask 可以被后续 CSE 合并。
- 在 CANN 9.0.0 及 beta.1 LLVM emitter 中，将 `1PT_B8/B16/B32` store 的无效 mask operand 替换为 `undef`；仅供 1PT store 使用的 `pset/pge` producer 不再生成 intrinsic，混合 NORM use 仍保留真实 mask。
- 新增 `vpto-mask-simplify`，消除输入均为 `PAT_ALL` 的 `pintlv/pdintlv`，覆盖 B8/B16/B32 以及 `pset/pge` 组合，并保留非全真重排。
- 按 layout fact 为多 chunk 的 lane-stride narrowing 分类赋予独立 cast seed phase，并沿合法 cast relation 自然传播；普通 widening 不设全局 anchor，`Reduce` 等更高优先级消费者仍可直接决定 widen 结果布局。

## 回归覆盖

- `f32 -> f16/f8 -> f32`、signed/unsigned integer 2x/4x roundtrip 不再在窄化与扩展之间插入 `ensure_layout`。
- `i16 -> i32 -> group_reduce(group=8)` 直接生成消费者需要的 `deinterleaved=4` widen 结果，不再在 widen 后生成 `vintlv/vdintlv`。
- f8 compute 路径采用 `UNPK4 + P0 vcvt`，不再生成 `vintlv`。
- 连续 group load 覆盖 bf16、ui8、si16、f32，64/128/256 lanes 和 group 4/8/16，并包含动态及非连续负例。
- mask 覆盖两套 LLVM emitter、B8/B16/B32、纯 1PT 与 1PT/NORM 混合 use、全真与非全真重排。
- 新增完整动态双缓冲 fused quant-dequant 优化守护，覆盖 `DINTLV_B16` 连续 group load、8-slot reciprocal 的直接寄存器 group broadcast、无 `VST_VLD`/`E2B_B16` 的 quant/dequant FP8 roundtrip，以及 `pset` mask canonicalization。

## 测试

- 增量构建：`pto-test-opt`、`PTOASCompiler` 通过。
- 定向 layout/pass/emitter lit：6/6 通过。
- `vmi_new/opt` lit：7/7 通过。
- 完整 `vmi_new/` lit：457/457 通过。
- 完整 `vpto/` lit：442/448 通过。6 个失败分别为缺少 `pto-vfsimt-size-patcher-test`、4 个 TileLib 常量 SSA 顺序 FileCheck、1 个 soft-postupdate 算术顺序 FileCheck，均不经过本 PR 修改路径。
- CANN 9.0.0 和 9.0.0-beta.1 的 1PT B8/B16/B32 LLVM IR 此前均已使用 Bisheng 编译为无残留 `llvm.hivm.*` 符号的 AICore relocatable object。
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` 通过。

title: [VMI] Cover generalized group-slot integer extensions
body:
## 背景

主线已经具备 group-slot 整数扩宽 lowering，但已有回归主要集中在 `num_groups=8` 的少数组合，无法系统证明 `ui8 -> ui16` 属于完整的通用能力，而不是单一 dtype 特判。

## 改动

- 新增正交能力矩阵，覆盖：
  - `extui` 的 unsigned 类型与 `extsi` 的 signed/signless 类型，包括 mixed `si/i` 结果；
  - `8 -> 16`、`16 -> 32`、`8 -> 32` 三种扩宽关系；
  - `slots=1` 同布局，以及 `slots=8` 的自然 `lane_stride=2/4` 输入；
  - `num_groups=1/2/4/8`，并用 `16/32` 验证跨越单个物理 carrier 后的 2-part/4-part lowering。
- 在现有 group-slot load 测试中补充 pointer-ABI 的 `ui8 -> ui16` 链路：
  - compact `slots=8` load 先通过 `ensure_layout` 形成自然 `lane_stride=2`，再扩宽并 group store；
  - `slots=1` load、扩宽和 group store 的完整链路。
- 新增负向边界，明确拒绝错误 signedness、缺少自然 stride 的 compact 直接扩宽，以及与扩宽倍数不一致的 stride。

本 PR 只补齐主线现有通用能力的回归覆盖，不重复修改 lowering。compact `slots=8` 数据需要先物化为自然 lane stride；未指定布局的整图 seed phase 优化由 #1114 处理。

## 验证

- `cmake --build build -j64`
- 定向 lit：3/3 passed
- `vmi_new` lit：452/452 passed

关联 learning-chip/vmi-demo#30

title: [Bug] [PTODSL] [阻塞] FP32 标量 lowering 未经 fastmath 请求收缩 FMA，且 divf 存在 1 ULP 差异
body:
### Component

Python bindings (python/)

### Description

SIMT FP32 标量算术存在两类精度语义差异：

1. PTODSL 生成独立的 `arith.mulf` 和 `arith.addf`，且没有设置
   `fastmath`/`contract`，但最终运行结果与融合的 `fmaf` 完全一致。
2. SIMT 标量 `arith.divf` 与 PyTorch NPU FP32 除法存在约 1 ULP 差异，
   当前也没有类似 Tile `tdiv` 的 high-precision 标量接口可供选择。

### Reproduction (minimal)

```markdown
import ctypes

import torch
import torch_npu
from ptodsl import pto


N = 256

torch.npu.config.allow_internal_format = False
torch_npu.npu.set_compile_mode(jit_compile=False)
torch.npu.set_device("npu:0")


@pto.simt(max_threads=N)
def div_simt(
    lhs: pto.ptr(pto.f32, "gm"),
    rhs: pto.ptr(pto.f32, "gm"),
    dst: pto.ptr(pto.f32, "gm"),
):
    tid = pto.get_tid_x()
    pto.stg(pto.ldg(lhs, tid) / pto.ldg(rhs, tid), dst, tid)


@pto.jit(
    name="simt_div_probe",
    kernel_kind="vector",
    target="a5",
    backend="vpto",
    mode="explicit",
)
def div_kernel(
    lhs: pto.ptr(pto.f32, "gm"),
    rhs: pto.ptr(pto.f32, "gm"),
    dst: pto.ptr(pto.f32, "gm"),
):
    div_simt[N, 1, 1](lhs, rhs, dst)


@pto.simt(max_threads=N)
def muladd_simt(
    a: pto.ptr(pto.f32, "gm"),
    b: pto.ptr(pto.f32, "gm"),
    c: pto.ptr(pto.f32, "gm"),
    dst: pto.ptr(pto.f32, "gm"),
):
    tid = pto.get_tid_x()
    pto.stg(
        pto.ldg(c, tid) + pto.ldg(a, tid) * pto.ldg(b, tid),
        dst,
        tid,
    )


@pto.jit(
    name="simt_muladd_probe",
    kernel_kind="vector",
    target="a5",
    backend="vpto",
    mode="explicit",
)
def muladd_kernel(
    a: pto.ptr(pto.f32, "gm"),
    b: pto.ptr(pto.f32, "gm"),
    c: pto.ptr(pto.f32, "gm"),
    dst: pto.ptr(pto.f32, "gm"),
):
    muladd_simt[N, 1, 1](a, b, c, dst)


def mismatch_count(actual, expected):
    return int(
        (actual.view(torch.int32) != expected.view(torch.int32)).sum()
    )


stream = torch.npu.current_stream()._as_parameter_

# divf
torch.manual_seed(20260803)

lhs_host = torch.rand(N, dtype=torch.float32) * 2
rhs_host = torch.rand(N, dtype=torch.float32) * 128 + 0.25

lhs = lhs_host.to("npu:0")
rhs = rhs_host.to("npu:0")
div_output = torch.empty_like(lhs)

compiled_div = div_kernel.compile()
compiled_div[1, stream](
    lhs.data_ptr(),
    rhs.data_ptr(),
    div_output.data_ptr(),
)
torch.npu.synchronize()

actual_div = div_output.cpu()
expected_div = (lhs / rhs).cpu()

print(
    "div mismatch:",
    mismatch_count(actual_div, expected_div),
    "/",
    N,
)
print(
    "div max abs:",
    float((actual_div - expected_div).abs().max()),
)

# mulf + addf
torch.manual_seed(20260803)

a_host = torch.randn(N, dtype=torch.float32)
b_host = torch.randn(N, dtype=torch.float32)
c_host = torch.randn(N, dtype=torch.float32)

a = a_host.to("npu:0")
b = b_host.to("npu:0")
c = c_host.to("npu:0")
muladd_output = torch.empty_like(a)

compiled_muladd = muladd_kernel.compile()
compiled_muladd[1, stream](
    a.data_ptr(),
    b.data_ptr(),
    c.data_ptr(),
    muladd_output.data_ptr(),
)
torch.npu.synchronize()

actual_muladd = muladd_output.cpu()
separate_muladd = (c + a * b).cpu()

libm = ctypes.CDLL("libm.so.6")
fmaf = libm.fmaf
fmaf.argtypes = [
    ctypes.c_float,
    ctypes.c_float,
    ctypes.c_float,
]
fmaf.restype = ctypes.c_float

fused_muladd = torch.tensor(
    [
        fmaf(float(x), float(y), float(z))
        for x, y, z in zip(a_host, b_host, c_host)
    ],
    dtype=torch.float32,
)

print(
    "mul+add vs separate mismatch:",
    mismatch_count(actual_muladd, separate_muladd),
    "/",
    N,
)
print(
    "mul+add vs fmaf mismatch:",
    mismatch_count(actual_muladd, fused_muladd),
    "/",
    N,
)

# 查看 PTODSL 生成的 MLIR
mlir_text = muladd_kernel.compile().mlir_text()
for line in mlir_text.splitlines():
    if "mulf" in line or "addf" in line or "fastmath" in line:
        print(line)
```

### Expected behavior

1. 当 MLIR 中只有独立的 arith.mulf 和 arith.addf，且没有fastmath<contract> 时，后端应保留两次独立舍入，不应自动收缩为 FMA。
2. 如果 PTOAS 设计上允许默认收缩，应提供显式控制开关，并明确记录数值语义。
3. SIMT FP32 标量除法应提供正确舍入或 high-precision 模式，类似 Tile tdiv(..., div_precision=...) 的能力。
4. 应增加 A5 VPTO 端到端运行测试，逐位验证：
  - 独立 mulf + addf
  - 显式 pto.fma
  - 标量 arith.divf
  - high-precision 标量除法

### Actual behavior / error logs

```text
div mismatch: 22 / 256
div max abs: 2.9802322387695312e-08

mul+add vs separate mismatch: 61 / 256
mul+add vs fmaf mismatch: 0 / 256


%7 = arith.mulf %4, %6 : f32
%8 = arith.addf %2, %7 : f32
```

### Git commit

7fd64fe21a403ae85288d8bcdeef34cb333f985

### Host platform

None

### Target Ascend arch (if relevant)

None

### PTOAS build level (if relevant)

None

title: [Pass Bug] level2 insert-sync guards only the first multi_tile_get of an iteration; a second co-live slot is left unsynchronized
body:
## Summary

At `--pto-level=level2 --enable-insert-sync`, when a loop body performs **two**
`pto.multi_tile_get` on the same `!pto.multi_tile_buf` region, ptoas emits the
per-slot dynamic WAR pair (`wait_flag`/`set_flag` on a derived `event_t`) for the
**first** access only. The second slot's `TLOAD` is emitted with **no preceding
`wait_flag` at all**, so the next iteration's write into that slot races the
current iteration's read of it.

The result is a silently wrong kernel on device — not a missed optimization.

Related to but distinct from #1106 (that one is a level3 address-folding issue;
this one is a level2 sync-derivation gap).

## Environment

- ptoas **v0.54** (aarch64), `--enable-insert-sync --pto-level=level2 --pto-arch a3`
- Device: Ascend a2a3
- `--enable-graph-sync-solver` behaves the same.

## Reproducer

Input `.pto` (trimmed — one region, two gets per iteration, both slot indices
affine in the loop variable):

```mlir
%ub_mb = pto.alloc_multi_tile valid_row = %c64_index valid_col = %c64_index
       : !pto.multi_tile_buf<!pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f32, rows=64, cols=64,
                                           v_row=?, v_col=?, blayout=row_major,
                                           slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>, count=2>
scf.for %i = %c0_index to %c4_index step %c1_index {
  %0  = arith.remsi %i, %c2_index : index                 // i % 2
  %lo = pto.multi_tile_get %ub_mb[%0]  : ... -> !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, ...>
  pto.tload ins(%a_view ...) outs(%lo : ...)
  %3  = arith.addi %i, %c1_index : index
  %4  = arith.remsi %3, %c2_index : index                 // (i + 1) % 2
  %hi = pto.multi_tile_get %ub_mb[%4]  : ... -> !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, ...>
  pto.tload ins(%b_view ...) outs(%hi : ...)
  %s  = pto.tadd ins(%lo, %hi : ...) outs(%s : ...)       // both slots read here
  pto.tstore ins(%s ...) outs(%out_view ...)
}
```

## Emitted code (v0.54)

```cpp
// prologue — BOTH event ids are primed, so the region's slot count is understood
set_flag(PIPE_V, PIPE_MTE2, EVENT_ID0);
set_flag(PIPE_V, PIPE_MTE2, EVENT_ID1);

for (int64_t i11 = v8; i11 < v5; i11 += v6) {
  int64_t v12 = i11 % v4;
  uint64_t v14 = (uint64_t)(v12 == v6 ? v9 : v8);
  TASSIGN(v13, v14);                              // lo -> slot i % 2

  int64_t  v20 = (int64_t)((uint64_t)v12 % (uint64_t)v4) == v6 ? v6 : v8;
  event_t  v21 = (event_t) v20;                   // dynamic id derived from lo's slot
  wait_flag(PIPE_V, PIPE_MTE2, v21);              // <-- guards lo
  TLOAD(v13, v19);

  uint64_t v23 = (uint64_t)((int64_t)((uint64_t)i11 + (uint64_t)v6) % v4 == v6 ? v9 : v8);
  TASSIGN(v22, v23);                              // hi -> slot (i + 1) % 2
  TLOAD(v22, v26);                                // <-- NO wait_flag before this load

  set_flag(PIPE_MTE2, PIPE_V, EVENT_ID0);
  wait_flag(PIPE_MTE2, PIPE_V, EVENT_ID0);
  TADD(v27, v13, v22);                            // reads BOTH slots

  event_t v29 = (event_t) v20;
  set_flag(PIPE_V, PIPE_MTE2, v29);               // <-- releases lo's slot only
  ...
}
```

`EVENT_ID1` is primed in the prologue and then never waited on or set inside the
loop: only one of the two slots is ever guarded.

## Observed failure

`out = a + b` over 4 row-blocks of `[64, 64]` fp32, with distinct per-element
inputs. Expected `out[k] = a[k] + b[k]`; measured

```
out[k] = a[block i+1][k] + a[block i][k]
```

i.e. iteration *i+1*'s `lo` load into slot 1 landed before iteration *i*'s `TADD`
had read slot 1 as `hi`. Exactly the missing WAR edge.

## What does work

- **One `multi_tile_get` per iteration** (the ordinary ping-pong) is guarded
  correctly — dynamic `wait_flag`/`set_flag` pair present, numerically correct on
  device. This is the shape we ship.
- **Straight-line code** with two constant slots: no loop, no cross-iteration
  reuse, correct.
- An **Acc/L0C** region with two co-live slots happens to be correct, but not via
  per-slot ids — ptoas falls back to a single static `wait_flag(PIPE_FIX, PIPE_M,
  EVENT_ID0)` placed after both drains, which serializes conservatively.

## Expected behaviour

Every `multi_tile_get` of a region in an iteration should receive its own
per-slot WAR guard (or, failing that, a conservative guard) — never no guard at
all.

## Impact on PyPTO

PyPTO now **refuses** to lower a slotted allocation with two slots live inside one
loop body under `memory_planner=PTOAS`, and points the author at the PyPTO memory
planner instead. We would like to lift that restriction once this is fixed; on our
side it is a single condition in `PTOCodegen::PlanMultiBufferRegions`, with no
user-facing API change.

title: [Bug] [PTODSL] [阻塞] PTOAS/PTODSL 适配 PIPE_MTE1 不在白名单里
body:
### Component

PTO Dialect / ODS (include/PTO/IR)

### Description

## 问题究竟在哪
### 核心结论：
同步逻辑本身正确，问题是 TileLang、PTODSL、PTOAS 三层对 mode 4 同步能力的定义不一致。

### 1. 同步拓扑没有问题
PTO 与 AscendC 的代码已经逐项对比：
Cube set  PIPE_MTE1(p / p+16)
    ↔ Vector wait PIPE_MTE3(p)

Vector set PIPE_MTE3(p+2)
    ↔ Cube wait PIPE_MTE1(p+2 / p+18)
pipe、event、+16 sid 映射、执行顺序均一致，也符合 CANN A5 的 1 Cube + 2 Vector 协议。
因此不应该修改：
barrier.cc 调度逻辑
pipe 端点
event ID
+16 映射
prologue/epilogue
set/wait 顺序
### 2. 第一处问题：白名单能力缺口
当前源码存在三层不一致：
TileLang mode 4 codegen 不允许 PIPE_MTE1
PTOAS A5 SyncSetOp 只允许 PIPE_FIX/PIPE_MTE3
CANN/Bisheng 实际支持：
set_intra_block(PIPE_MTE1, event_id);
所以这是 verifier/API 没覆盖真实硬件能力，不是硬件不支持。
### 3. 第二处问题：动态 event 类型没有转换
仅放开白名单后，动态调用仍会失败：
expects Value, got RuntimeValue
TileLang 当前直接生成：
_tl_pto_ops.sync_wait(pipe, dynamic_event)
但 dynamic_event 是 PTODSL RuntimeValue，raw PTO op 需要 MLIR Value。
静态 event 是 Python int，所以静态的 0/1/16/17 可以正常建立；第一次动态 wait 才暴露问题。
### 4. 不是 PTOAS 自动插入同步
虽然 kernel 带有 insert_sync=True，但函数已经存在显式 set_flag/wait_flag，PTOAS InsertSync 会直接跳过。
并且 InsertSync 不生成本次涉及的 cross-core sync.set/sync.wait。PIPE_MTE1 来自 TileLang scheduler，不是 PTOAS 底层添加的。
最合理、最安全的修改方法
建议只修改三个窄点。
#### 1. PTOAS verifier
A5 SyncSetOp 白名单改为：
PIPE_FIX
PIPE_MTE1
PIPE_MTE3
SyncWaitOp 保持现有：
PIPE_FIX
PIPE_MTE1
PIPE_MTE2
PIPE_MTE3
PIPE_V
只增加已经被本算子、AscendC 和 CANN 证明需要的 PIPE_MTE1。不要顺便放开未经验证的其他 set pipe。
#### 2. PTODSL 公共接口
让 facade 与 verifier 完全一致：
set_intra_flag:
    FIX, MTE1, MTE3

wait_intra_flag:
    FIX, MTE1, MTE2, MTE3, V
该接口已有正确的动态值处理：
unwrap_surface_value(event_id)
因此应该让这一层统一负责 RuntimeValue 转换和 event 范围检查。
#### 3. TileLang codegen
mode 4 不再直接生成 raw _tl_pto_ops.sync_*，而是生成：
pto.set_intra_flag(pipe, event_id)
pto.wait_intra_flag(pipe, event_id)
同时使用 set/wait 各自的白名单：
set : FIX, MTE1, MTE3
wait: FIX, MTE1, MTE2, MTE3, V
这样：
动态 event 自动解包
静态 [0,31] 校验集中在 PTODSL
TileLang、PTODSL、PTOAS 三层契约完全一致
每个原始同步仍严格对应一个 PTO 同步

title: fix(tile-fusion): disable A5 op fusion by default
feat: unify TFILLPAD modes and FP operand forms
body:
## Summary

- Collapse `pto.tfillpad_inplace` and `pto.tfillpad_expand` into `pto.tfillpad`; PTOAS infers Normal, InPlace, or Expand after physical-shape analysis and memory planning. The textual op does not accept a `mode` attribute.
- Make the VPTO Normal fallback alias-safe by copying the complete valid source region before padding, matching the EmitC/PTO-ISA ordering when equality cannot be proven.
- Remove the textual IR ops `pto.textract_fp`, `pto.tinsert_fp`, `pto.tmov.fp`, and `pto.tstore_fp`; represent FP variants through optional `fp` operands on the unified ops.
- Keep one-to-one PTO-ISA lowering: no-mode FP forms select `TEXTRACT_FP`, `TINSERT_FP`, `TMOV_FP`, and `TSTORE_FP`, while explicit A5 acc-to-vec modes select the unified PTO-ISA overloads.
- Preserve PTO-BC v0 cross-build safety: historical FP and tfillpad wire opcodes remain readable, but legacy FP opcodes are emitted only when the old op can express every semantic field and has no result. Extended resultless `tmov + fp` uses generic v0; result-bearing `tmov + fp` and extended/result-bearing `tstore + fp` are rejected because there is no end-to-end legacy-safe lowering path.
- Classify ACC-to-VEC `pto.textract` as `PIPE_FIX`, with a lit test pinning the required `PIPE_FIX -> PIPE_V` synchronization.
- Migrate Python bindings, PTODSL, TileLib, tests, samples, documentation, and PTOBC metadata; add the PTO-BC suite and a pinned pre-unification reader/lowering compatibility check to CI.
- Update all seven managed PTO-ISA pin locations to `27386d906e8fdcbd93aec84197939bc0b2c6caea`; extend `update_pto_isa_pin.py` and its workflow to cover `ci_sim.yml` and the compile-only guide.

## Compatibility

- Existing `pto.tfillpad` source remains valid, but explicit `mode` attributes and the removed mode-specific textual op names must be dropped; lowering mode is compiler-inferred.
- Removed FP textual op names require migration to the corresponding unified op with an optional `fp` operand.
- PTO-BC v0 remains a cross-build exchange format. Legacy FP and tfillpad bytecode stays readable and is normalized to unified operations during decode.
- Writers never reuse a resultless legacy opcode when doing so would drop semantics in an older reader: extended resultless `tmov + fp` retains mode/relu through generic v0; result-bearing `tmov + fp` fails encoding because current PTOAS backends cannot lower that result; result-bearing non-FP `tstore` uses generic v0; extended/result-bearing `tstore + fp` fails encoding explicitly instead of producing silently lossy bytecode.

## Validation

- `PTOASPythonPackage` and `ptobc` builds passed.
- Full lit suite after merging current `main`: 1690 passed, 1 unsupported.
- PTO-BC suite: 22/22 passed, including legacy tfillpad opcode decode, unified FP operand round trips, extended FP generic encoding plus current PTOAS lowering, and explicit result-bearing/lossy FP rejection.
- New writer -> pre-unification `0.56` reader -> pre-unification lowering passed at commit `9c49c3697de35d4b36e2abc5a00da0b264ae1bb6`; the generated TMOV retains `SingleModeVec0` and `NormalRelu`, and the simple TSTORE still lowers as `TSTORE_FP`.
- Fillpad samples passed for Normal, Expand, and InPlace; invalid cases produced the expected XFAIL results.
- Focused tfillpad/ACC-to-VEC sync lit tests: 3/3 passed.
- `git diff --check`, changed-range clang-format, shell syntax, ShellCheck, actionlint, and PTO-BC schema checks passed.

title: [Bug] [阻塞] vstus emitter 生成固定裸名 llvm.hivm.vstus，同 kernel 内多类型混用导致 conflicting declaration
body:
### Component

PTO Dialect / ODS (include/PTO/IR)

### Description

buildVstusCallee（VPTOCANN900LLVMEmitter.cpp:2301、VPTOLLVMEmitter.cpp:2345）对所有 pto.vstus 调用都生成固定裸名 llvm.hivm.vstus（无类型后缀）。当同一个 kernel 内出现不同 value 类型的 vstus 调用时（如 ui8 + f32），LLVM 模块内同名函数出现不同参数签名，触发 conflicting declaration 编译错误。


### Reproduction (minimal)

```markdown
复现步骤
1. 写一个最小 ptodsl kernel，内含两种类型的 vstus：
@pto.jit(name="demo_vstus_conflict", target="a5", kernel_kind="vector")
def _k():
    st = pto.alloc_tile(shape=[1, 128], dtype=pto.f32, valid_shape=[1, 128])
    dt_f32 = pto.alloc_tile(shape=[1, 128], dtype=pto.f32, valid_shape=[1, 128])
    dt_u8 = pto.alloc_tile(shape=[1, 128], dtype=pto.ui8, valid_shape=[1, 128])
    src_ptr = st.as_ptr()
    dst_f32_ptr = dt_f32.as_ptr()
    dst_u8_ptr = dt_u8.as_ptr()
    v_f32 = pto.vlds(src_ptr, 0)
    v_u8 = pto.vbitcast(v_f32, pto.ui8)
    ureg1 = pto.init_align()
    ureg1 = pto.vstus(ureg1, 1, v_f32, dst_f32_ptr)       # f32 vstus
    pto.vstas(ureg1, pto.addptr(dst_f32_ptr, 1), 0)
    ureg2 = pto.init_align()
    ureg2 = pto.vstus(ureg2, 1, v_u8, dst_u8_ptr)          # ui8 vstus
    pto.vstas(ureg2, pto.addptr(dst_u8_ptr, 1), 0)
    pto.pipe_barrier(pto.Pipe.ALL)
2. 生成 MLIR 并用 ptoas 编译：
ptoas --pto-arch=a5 --enable-insert-sync --enable-tile-op-expand \
  kernel.mlir -o kernel.o
```

### Expected behavior

编译通过

### Actual behavior / error logs

```text
VPTO LLVM emission failed: conflicting declaration for llvm.hivm.vstus
Error: Failed to lower VPTO to LLVM modules.

title: feat(vpto): add AICore ld_dev and st_dev ops
body:
## 背景

普通 AICore 的 scalar GM data-cache bypass 与 SIMT `pto.ldg` / `pto.stg` 属于不同执行域和 intrinsic 家族。此前普通 `pto.aicore` 函数中的误用会通过 PTO verifier，随后使 Bisheng 在 device LLVM 编译阶段崩溃。

Closes #1032

## 主要变更

- 先补齐现有 `pto.ldg` / `pto.stg` 的 placement verifier，只允许其位于 `pto.simt_entry` 或 `pto.section.simt`。
- 新增独立的普通 AICore micro-op：`pto.ld_dev` 与 `pto.st_dev`，不继承 SIMT op。
- 首版接口仅支持 `!pto.ptr<T, gm>` 与 `T = i8/i16/i32/i64`；offset 为元素步长，load result/store value 必须与指针元素类型一致。
- 固定绕过本地 L1 data cache，不接受 `l1cache` / `l2cache` policy 属性，也不隐含 atomic、同步、内存序、invalidate 或 writeback 语义。
- 将 element offset 先 lower 为 typed GEP，再调用 offset 为 0 的 `llvm.hivm.LD.DEV.u*.GM` / `llvm.hivm.ST.DEV.u*`。
- 仅在 A5 且 CANN output version 9.0.0 official 或更新版本开放；A2/A3 与 9.0.0-beta.1 在进入 Bisheng 前给出明确诊断。
- 保持 Group 14 为纯 shared `arith`、Group 17 为 SIMT；新增 Group 18 `Special Scalar Operations`，收录 10 个 PTO scalar kernel query、pointer/address 与 scalar-memory op。
- 将 Group 18 从操作目录扩展为可独立阅读的手册：逐项说明 purpose、完整 syntax、operand/result/attribute、类型与地址空间约束、offset 单位、语义伪代码、execution scope、target gating 和示例。
- `docs/vpto-spec.md` 保留总体说明和索引，同一批 scalar op 的重复逐项定义改为链接到 Group 18，避免两处规范成为不同真源。

## 测试

- `cmake --build build --target PTOASPythonPackage -j16`
- 5 个聚焦 VPTO lit 全部通过，覆盖 verifier、SIMT placement、i8/i16/i32/i64 LLVM emission、动态/静态 element offset 及 target/version gating；这些 compiler regression tests 不依赖 CANN 工具链。
- `test/vpto/scripts/run_host_vpto_validation.sh` 的 `micro-op/scalar-load-store/ld-st-dev` A5 simulator case 通过 fatobj/device-object emission、host build、runtime 与 golden compare。
- 文档改动通过 `git diff --check`，并检查 Group 18 恰好包含 10 个 PTO scalar op 的独立手册小节，`docs/vpto-spec.md` 不再重复定义这些 op。

Runtime 与 object compilation 当前覆盖 i32 非零 offset roundtrip；i8/i16/i32/i64 四种宽度均由 LLVM emission 用例覆盖。

title: [Bug] ast_rewrite branch merge 类型不匹配：bool buffer load 返回 i8，条件变量期望 i1
body:
### Component

Verifier / IR semantics (lib/PTO/IR)

### Description

PTODSL 的 ast_rewrite 在 branch merge 时，如果 then 分支从 bool buffer 读取值（`scalar.load` 返回 i8），else 分支是 i1 常量（`pto.const(0, dtype=pto.i1)`），会报类型不匹配错误：

```
RuntimeError: br.assign(...) type mismatch for 'cond': then branch yields i8, else branch yields i1
```

### Reproduction (minimal)

```markdown
from ptodsl import pto, scalar

@pto.jit(name="repro_bool_merge", target="a5")
def kernel(flag: pto.ptr(pto.i8, "gm")) -> pto.i32:
    cond = pto.const(0, dtype=pto.i1)

    if pto.const(1, dtype=pto.i32):
        cond = scalar.load(flag, 0)

    if cond:
        return pto.const(42, dtype=pto.i32)
    return pto.const(0, dtype=pto.i32)

print(kernel.compile().mlir_text())
```

### Expected behavior

ast_rewrite 在 branch merge 时，如果 then/else 分支类型不一致但可以安全转换（如 i8→i1 的非零语义），应自动插入转换（如 `cond != 0` 或等价的 i1 转换），而不是直接报错。

### Actual behavior / error logs

```text
RuntimeError: br.assign(...) type mismatch for 'cond': then branch yields i8, else branch yields i1
```

body:
## Summary

- mark `comm_p2p` and `comm_p2p_binding_variants` entry functions as vector kernels
- keep PTOAS fence lowering consistent with the `dav-c220-vec` architecture selected by A3 board validation
- prevent these samples from emitting `pipe_barrier(PIPE_FIX)` in vector kernels

## Root cause

PR #1033 made vector GM fences lower to `pipe_barrier(PIPE_ALL); dsb(DSB_DDR);`, but the two Python sample builders only set `pto.entry`. Without `pto.kernel_kind = #pto.kernel_kind<vector>`, EmitC lowering treated them as non-vector and emitted the conservative MTE2/MTE3/FIX sequence. The board generator independently selected `dav-c220-vec`, so the generated `PIPE_FIX` barrier caused an AIV illegal-instruction failure.

## Validation

- both Python sample builders compile and verify
- generated PTO IR contains `pto.kernel_kind = #pto.kernel_kind<vector>`
- generated C++ contains `pipe_barrier(PIPE_ALL); dsb(DSB_DDR);`
- generated C++ contains no `pipe_barrier(PIPE_FIX)`
- `git diff --check` passes
- A3 runtime retest is pending because the available board account currently lacks access to `/dev/davinci*`

## Related

- #953
- #1026
- #1033
